source.title: The supercuspidal representations of p-adic classical groups
source.versionRead: The author's accepted version, arXiv:math/0607622v2 (12 November 2007, 'minor changes from 1st version (mostly in sections 2.2, 4.2 and 6.2). To appear in Inventiones mathematicae, 2008'), read completely in its LaTeX source with the 55-page PDF for page locators; the published article is paywalled and was not read, so every locator and finding is scoped to arXiv v2 (with v1 compared where relevant). Locators give section, numbered statement and arXiv v2 PDF page.

readSections: §1 A variant of a result of L. Morris (pp. 5–6)
§3 Semisimple characters and Heisenberg extensions, including characters of Sylow subgroups and the analogous results for G̃ (pp. 13–19)
§4 Beta extensions, maximal and general cases (pp. 19–25)
§5 Iwahori factorizations: decompositions, factorization of semisimple characters, Glauberman transfer (pp. 25–34)
§6 Intertwining and supercuspidal representations: a Hecke algebra isomorphism, Weyl group elements, intertwining of β-extensions, supercuspidal types (pp. 34–44)
§7 Exhaustion: a Hecke algebra injection, covers, conclusions (pp. 44–53); bibliography (pp. 53–55)
Every statement and proof was read line by line in the TeX; v1 was diffed against v2 section by section.

summary: Stevens proves that, for a non-archimedean local field F of odd residual characteristic and G a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group over F₀, every irreducible supercuspidal representation of G is compactly induced from an explicit cuspidal type (Theorem 7.14), and that every such type induces irreducibly to a supercuspidal (Proposition 6.18, Corollary 6.19). The types are built from skew semisimple strata and characters, their Heisenberg representations, β-extensions (§4) and cuspidal representations of finite reductive quotients, using Iwahori factorizations and Glauberman transfer (§5), an intertwining computation with Weyl-group elements (§6) and a cover/Hecke-algebra argument based on Morris's level-zero theory (§§1, 7). Miyauchi–Stevens (Math. Ann. 2014) later corrected Definition 6.5, Corollary 6.19 and Theorem 7.14 (maximal-parahoric and compact-centre conditions, and the exclusion of SO(1,1)); the items use the corrected statements. Of 302 items (after the review merged three pairs and this repair merged disconnected-cuspidality item 306 into 246), 6 are in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (the base field, Mackey formula and irreducibility criterion, Clifford's theorem, Frobenius reciprocity, intertwining spaces) and 8 are planned (compact induction and supercuspidality in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2–SR.3, buildings and parahorics in ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2, projective extension in Tau Ceti's InductionRestriction). The other 288 — the whole classical-group type theory — are missing: 280 go to the accepted Part II SmoothRepresentationsPartII (types, depth and supercuspidal constructions), as its classical-group branch beside Fintzen's tame p ∤ |W| construction, and 2 finite Heisenberg lemmas to FiniteWeilRepresentationsPartII, and (moved by the review) six facts about finite reductive groups to ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. 55 source findings are recorded (twelve added by the independent review, with the verified skew-scalar wording added as E55 in this repair): 7 are corrections already published by Miyauchi–Stevens (including the 4 that affect stated results: the introduction's ellipticity claim, Corollary 6.19, Theorem 7.14 and Definition 6.5), and 48 are new, mostly misprints in proofs.

items.name: Base field: a non-archimedean local field with involution, odd residual characteristic
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field (locally compact; the characteristic of F may be 0 or p), equipped with a galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; F = F₀ (trivial involution) is allowed. o_F, p_F, k_F = o_F/p_F are its ring of integers, maximal ideal and residue field, and throughout the residual characteristic p := char k_F is not 2. o₀, p₀, k₀ denote the same objects for F₀; similar notation is used for any non-archimedean local field.
items.locator: Introduction, p. 2 ('a non-archimedean local field F of odd residual characteristic with a (possibly trivial) galois involution with fixed field F₀'); §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 827-833); abstract ('locally compact')
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LocalField/Basic.lean:45 `class IsNonarchimedeanLocalField (K) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] : Prop extends IsValuativeTopology K, LocallyCompactSpace K, ValuativeRel.IsNontrivial K` (no characteristic restriction, matching the paper). The fixed field of the involution is `FixedPoints.subfield M F` (Mathlib/FieldTheory/Fixed.lean:103, for a monoid M acting by ring automorphisms, here the group of order ≤ 2 generated by the involution). The hypothesis p ≠ 2 is a plain hypothesis on the residue field. Only the setting is library; nothing about it is proved here. Fintzen's branch uses the same kind of field (arbitrary characteristic) but assumes p ∤ |W|, much stronger than p odd for classical groups (|W| = 2ⁿn! for Sp_2n).

items.name: Normalized uniformizers ϖ_F and ϖ₀
items.statement: Fix a uniformizer ϖ_F of F with ϖ̄_F = −ϖ_F if F/F₀ is ramified and ϖ̄_F = ϖ_F otherwise; put ϖ₀ = ϖ_F² if F/F₀ is ramified and ϖ₀ = ϖ_F otherwise, so that ϖ₀ is a uniformizer of F₀. The same convention is used for every extension E/F to which the involution extends.
items.note: Mathlib has uniformizers for rank-one discrete valuations (`Valuation.IsUniformizer`, Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/Discrete/Basic.lean:199; existence `exists_isUniformizer_of_isCyclic_of_nontrivial`, line 296) but not the existence of a uniformizer that is an eigenvector of the involution. That existence uses p ≠ 2: a ramified quadratic F/F₀ is tame, so F = F₀(√(ϖ₀u)) and one can take ϖ_F with ϖ_F² ∈ F₀ a uniformizer; then ϖ̄_F = −ϖ_F and ϖ_F² is a uniformizer of F₀. In the unramified or trivial case ϖ_F ∈ F₀. Checked. No atlas layer states it (LocalFieldsRamification layer 0 supplies local fields and extensions only). Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: The ε-hermitian space and the groups G̃, G⁺, G, with the involution σ and A₋ ≅ Lie G
items.statement: V is an N-dimensional F-vector space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1; h is sesquilinear for the involution and h(w,v) = ε·h(v,w)‾; the paper does not fix which variable is conjugate-linear). A = End_F V, and a ↦ ā is the adjoint anti-involution of A defined by h. G̃ = Aut_F V; σ is the involution g ↦ ḡ⁻¹ of G̃ and a ↦ −ā of A; Σ = {1, σ}. G⁺ = G̃^Σ = {g ∈ G̃ : h(gv, gw) = h(v, w) for all v, w ∈ V}, the F₀-points of a unitary (F ≠ F₀), symplectic (F = F₀, ε = −1) or orthogonal (F = F₀, ε = +1) group 𝐆⁺ over F₀; G is the group of F₀-points of the identity component 𝐆 of 𝐆⁺, so G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G is special orthogonal. A₋ = A^Σ ≃ Lie G. Notation: S₋ = S^- = S ∩ A₋ for S ⊆ A, and H = H̃ ∩ G for H̃ ≤ G̃.
items.locator: Introduction, p. 2; §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 8 (TeX 842-863)
items.note: Pieces in the libraries, none giving the object: Mathlib sesquilinear forms `LinearMap.IsSymm` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:192, `∀ x y, I (B x y) = B y x`, i.e. hermitian for the ring map I; the ε = −1 case must be encoded separately), `LinearMap.Nondegenerate` (line 596), `LinearMap.IsAdjointPair` (line 373); the skew-adjoint Lie algebra `LinearMap.BilinForm.skewAdjointLieSubalgebra` (Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/SkewAdjoint.lean:60) exists only for bilinear forms; matrix groups for the standard forms only (`Matrix.symplecticGroup`, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean:101; `Matrix.orthogonalGroup`, `Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup`, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean:295, 315); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ConstantForm.groupScheme` (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/ConstantForm/Basic.lean:339: the subgroup scheme of GL_n of M with M C Mᵀ = C, bilinear Gram matrices only, no smoothness). Missing: the isometry group of an ε-hermitian form over F/F₀ as an F₀-group (needs restriction of scalars, planned in ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a), its identity component (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 3 plans identity components in general) and the identification A₋ ≃ Lie G. Fintzen's branch treats general tame reductive G, of which these are instances only when p ∤ |W|; it has no ε-hermitian presentation. Edge case: for F = F₀, ε = +1, N = 2 and h isotropic, G = SO(1,1)(F) ≅ F^× is a split torus; the paper does not exclude it, see issues PAPER-STEVENS-08/E1-PAPER-STEVENS-08/E3.

items.name: Additive characters ψ₀, ψ_F, ψ_A
items.statement: ψ₀ is a character of the additive group of F₀ with conductor p₀ (trivial on p₀, not on o₀); ψ_F = ψ₀ ∘ tr_{F/F₀}, a character of F with conductor p_F; ψ_A = ψ_F ∘ tr_{A/F}.
items.note: Mathlib has `AddChar` and `AddChar.IsPrimitive` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:61) but no conductor of an additive character of a local field; searched declaration names containing 'conductor' (only Dirichlet characters and orders). The claim that ψ_F has conductor p_F was checked: the different of F/F₀ is o_F or p_F (p odd), so tr_{F/F₀}(p_F) = p₀ and tr_{F/F₀}(o_F) = o₀. AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0 plans 'self-duality of local additive groups' for completions of number fields (characteristic 0) only, so it is not a plan for this item. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: [S4, Theorem 5.1]: every irreducible supercuspidal representation contains a skew semisimple character
items.statement: (Stevens, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005), Theorem 5.1, as quoted.) Let F be a non-archimedean local field (locally compact, of characteristic 0 or p) with residual characteristic p ≠ 2 and a (possibly trivial) galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀, let (V,h) be a finite-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε = ±1), let G⁺ be its isometry group and G the F₀-points of the identity component (a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group). Every irreducible supercuspidal representation π of G contains a skew semisimple character θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β) for some skew semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β] (for β = 0 this is the trivial character of P₁(Λ), i.e. level zero).
items.locator: Introduction, p. 4 ('From [32], we know already that any irreducible supercuspidal representation π contains a semisimple character θ'); used in §7.4, arXiv v2 p. 53 (TeX 4645); cited again in §7.3, arXiv v2 p. 53
items.note: Quoted from the literature (Stevens 2005 is not on arXiv; not re-read). Skew semisimple characters are defined in §3 of this paper (other chunk). The analogue 'every irreducible representation contains a datum' is PAPER-FINTZEN-21/18 (tame, p ∤ |W|), a different object; not covered. The §7 chunk may carry the same item; merge on this locator. The review merged the duplicate item numbered 301 into this one.

items.name: Generalized affine BN-pair (G, B, N) and its Weyl group W = Ω ⋉ W′
items.statement: (Notation of [M1] = Morris, Invent. Math. 114 (1993); independent of the rest of the paper.) 𝐆 is a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field F, G = 𝐆(F); 𝐓 a maximal F-split torus with normalizer 𝐍, T = 𝐓(F), N = 𝐍(F); B an Iwahori subgroup, the stabilizer of a chamber in the apartment of T in the enlarged Bruhat–Tits building. Then (G, B, N) is a generalized affine BN-pair; its generalized affine Weyl group W = N/(B ∩ N) is the semidirect product of a subgroup Ω and a normal subgroup W′, the affine Weyl group of a split affine root system Σ, and S ⊂ W′ is the set of fundamental reflections of a simple system of affine roots.
items.locator: §1, arXiv v2 p. 6 (TeX 711-726)
items.note: RG2.1: 'Build the affine root system and apartment from the valued datum'; RG2.2: buildings, facets, 'fixers'; RG2.4: 'Prove ... the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their exact generality'; Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 7: 'Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems ... useful for the p-adic representation-theory consumers, who can ask only for a BN-pair'. Library partial: `TauCeti.TitsSystem` (TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Basic.lean:48, a structure with subgroupB, subgroupN, simple reflections in N/(B ∩ N) that generate it, and the Tits axioms) with the Bruhat decomposition `bruhatCells_eq_univ` (TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Bruhat/Basic.lean:374). That structure demands that the simple reflections generate W, so a generalized BN-pair with Ω ≠ 1 is not an instance; no Iwahori subgroup of a p-adic group exists in either library (searched 'Iwahori', 'parahoric', 'building', 'apartment': no declarations). Fintzen's branch imports buildings and parahorics from RG2.2-RG2.3 as well (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/29).

items.name: Standard parahoric subgroups P_J, their pro-unipotent radicals U_J and reductive quotients M_J
items.statement: For a proper subset J ⊊ S, W_J is the subgroup of W generated by the reflections in J and N_J the corresponding subgroup of N; P_J = B N_J B is a subgroup of G, a standard parahoric subgroup. U_J is its pro-unipotent radical and M_J = P_J/U_J is (the group of points of) a connected reductive group over the residue field. U_B = U_∅ is the pro-unipotent radical of B = P_∅.
items.locator: §1, arXiv v2 p. 6 (TeX 728-747)
items.note: RG2.3: 'For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme with connected special fiber ... connected reductive quotient of the special fiber, pro-unipotent radical and reduction map'. The description P_J = B N_J B through the affine BN-pair is standard Tits-system theory (planned with PAPER-STEVENS-08/6). Not built in either library.

items.name: Morris's distinguished double coset representatives D_{J,K} and D′_{J,K}
items.statement: For J, K ⊆ S, Morris ([M1, §3.10], see also Variant 3.22) defines a (in general non-unique) set D_{J,K} of distinguished double coset representatives for W_J \ W / W_K; a set D′_{J,K} of inverse images in N of D_{J,K} is a set of distinguished double coset representatives for P_J \ G / P_K.
items.locator: §1, arXiv v2 p. 6 (TeX 732-739)
items.note: No parabolic subgroups or minimal double coset representatives for Coxeter groups in Mathlib (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coxeter/{Basic,Inversion,Length,Matrix}.lean) or Tau Ceti (TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/*: Artin, Bruhat, Length, Poincare, StrongExchange; grep for 'parabolic', 'doubleCoset': none). RG2.4 plans 'finiteness of compact-open double coset decompositions', not these representatives. The definition lives in [M1] (paywalled, not re-read). Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Hecke algebra H(ρ|K) and intertwining I_G(ρ|K)
items.statement: For ρ a representation of a compact (open) subgroup K of G, H(ρ|K) = End_G(c-Ind_K^G ρ) is the associated Hecke algebra and I_G(ρ|K), the intertwining of ρ, is the support of this Hecke algebra (the set of g ∈ G with Hom_{K ∩ gKg⁻¹}(ρ, ᵍρ) ≠ 0, in the standard identification with ρ-spherical functions). In the function model (as in [BK, §4.1]) H(G, λ) is the convolution algebra of compactly supported functions φ : G → End(λ^∨) with φ(kgk′) = λ^∨(k)φ(g)λ^∨(k′), and the support of H(G, λ) is I_G(λ|K).
items.locator: §1, arXiv v2 p. 6 (TeX 749-754); used throughout; function model with supports KyK used throughout §6, arXiv v2 pp. 34–44
items.note: SR.1 plans the ambient Hecke algebra of compactly supported locally constant functions and SR.2 compact induction with Frobenius reciprocity, but neither plans End_G(c-Ind ρ) as ρ-spherical functions or the intertwining set. The data/library-coverage.json audit records that Hecke rings exist for any Hecke pair (Mathlib `HeckeRing`, Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean:189; Tau Ceti double-coset rings) 'but none is instantiated for G(K_v) with a compact open subgroup'. The type Hecke algebra of compactly supported ρ-spherical functions is PAPER-FINTZEN-21/1b in the SmoothRepresentationsPartII proposal; its definition does not depend on tameness, so this item is covered by that branch once it exists. The review merged the duplicate item numbered 200 into this one.

items.name: Cuspidal representations of the finite reductive quotient M_J
items.statement: An irreducible representation of the finite reductive group M_J = P_J/U_J is cuspidal if it has no nonzero vectors fixed by the unipotent radical of any proper parabolic subgroup of M_J; ρ denotes its inflation to P_J.
items.locator: §1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (Proposition 1.1, Theorem 1.2); the definition is not restated in the paper
items.note: No declaration named '*cuspidal*' in either library. The same predicate is PAPER-FINTZEN-21/33 ('Cuspidality for a finite reductive quotient', missing, routed to SmoothRepresentationsPartII) — covered by Fintzen's branch, whose finite-field definition has no tameness restriction.

items.name: [M1, Lemma 3.21] (as used)
items.statement: For J ⊊ S, n ∈ D′_{J,J} with image w ∈ W, P = P_J and U′ = nU_Jn⁻¹: P ∩ U′ ⊆ U_{J∩wJ}; moreover the image of P ∩ U′ in M_J is the unipotent radical of the parabolic subgroup P_{J∩wJ}/U_J of M_J (proper when wJ ≠ J).
items.locator: §1, proof of Proposition 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 765-767); the second clause is the form in which Kurinczuk–Stevens (Crelle 764 (2020), arXiv:1509.02212, proof of their variant of [M1, Proposition 4.13]) quote the same lemma
items.note: Morris 1993 (paywalled) not re-read; the statement is recorded as the two later papers use it. Not in either library or the atlas. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: [M1, Proposition 4.13] (Morris's original statement)
items.statement: Let J ⊊ S, D′_{J,J} a set of distinguished double coset representatives for P_J \ G / P_J, n ∈ D′_{J,J} with projection w ∈ W, and ρ the inflation to P_J of a cuspidal representation of M_J. If n lies in the support of H(ρ|P_J) (n intertwines ρ), then wJ = J.
items.locator: §1, Remark after Proposition 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 762-764)
items.note: Quoted through the Remark ('the hypothesis there is that n lies in the support of H(ρ|P_J)'). Not in either library or the atlas. Not in Fintzen's branch (whose depth-zero input is Moy–Prasad 1996, not Morris).

items.name: Proposition 1.1 (variant of [M1, Proposition 4.13])
items.statement: Let (G, B, N) be as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/6, J ⊊ S, D′_{J,J} a set of distinguished double coset representatives for P_J \ G / P_J and n ∈ D′_{J,J}. Let ρ be the inflation to P_J of a cuspidal representation of M_J. If n lies in the support of H(ρ|U_B), i.e. n intertwines the restriction of ρ to the pro-p Iwahori subgroup U_B, then wJ = J, where w ∈ W is the projection of n.
items.locator: §1, Proposition 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 756-761); used in §6 (Proposition 6.14, Corollary 6.16; TeX 3734, 3766)
items.note: Proof checked: by PAPER-STEVENS-08/11, P ∩ U′ ⊆ U_{J∩wJ} ⊆ U_B, and U′ ⊆ U′_B = nU_Bn⁻¹, so P ∩ U′ ⊆ U_B ∩ U′_B; a nonzero φ ∈ Hom_{U_B∩U′_B}(ρ, ⁿρ) satisfies φ∘ρ(x) = φ for x ∈ P ∩ U′ (ⁿρ is trivial on U′), so ρ has nonzero (P ∩ U′)-coinvariants, hence invariants, under the unipotent radical of a proper parabolic of M_J when wJ ≠ J, contradicting cuspidality. The paper's proof ('replace every P ∩ P′ in Morris's proof by U_B ∩ U′_B') is by reference; Kurinczuk–Stevens (arXiv:1509.02212, Lemma 'Lemma11') give this direct argument, for P_K \ G / P_J and ℓ-modular coefficients. Not in either library or the atlas; not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Case (i): the Levi subgroup 𝔐_J attached to a non-maximal parahoric P_J
items.statement: If P = P_J is a non-maximal parahoric subgroup, let ᶜΦ_J be the closure of the root system generated by the gradients of the affine roots in J and 𝔐_J = 𝕸_J(F) the points of the corresponding reductive subgroup of 𝐆 ([M1, §3.15]). Then 𝔐_J ∩ P_J is a parahoric subgroup of 𝔐_J with reductive quotient M_J. With N_J = N ∩ 𝔐_J ∩ P_J, a set of representatives for {n ∈ N : wJ = J}/N_J can be taken in the normalizer N_N(𝔐_J ∩ P_J) of 𝔐_J ∩ P_J in N ([M1, §4.16]).
items.locator: §1, item (i) after Proposition 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 779-790)
items.note: The symbol N_J is reused: earlier it denotes the subgroup of N over W_J (TeX 730). Quoted from [M1] (not re-read). Levi subgroups in general are planned (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 7), not this construction. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Case (ii): a maximal parahoric is normalized by n, and its normalizer is compact
items.statement: If P = P_J is a maximal parahoric subgroup of G and n ∈ D′_{J,J} satisfies wJ = J, then n normalizes P ([M1, Appendix A.1]). As printed: 'In the classical groups we will be looking at, the G-normalizer of P is compact.' Corrected: this holds when the group (in the application, G_E) has compact centre; it fails when G_E has a factor SO(1,1)(F) ≅ F^×.
items.locator: §1, item (ii) after Proposition 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 791-795)
items.note: The compactness claim is false for a factor SO(1,1)(F) of G_E (β_i = 0, dim V^i = 2, h|V^i hyperbolic, G orthogonal): its maximal parahoric o_F^× has normalizer F^×. See issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E1 (reported by Miyauchi–Stevens 2014). Not in either library or the atlas. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 ([M1, Theorem 4.15]): intertwining of a depth-zero cuspidal representation
items.statement: Let J ⊊ S and ρ the inflation to P_J of a cuspidal representation of M_J. Then I_G(ρ|P_J) ⊆ P_J N_N(ρ) P_J, where N_N(ρ) = {n ∈ N_N(𝔐_J ∩ P_J) : ⁿρ ≃ ρ}.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.2, arXiv v2 p. 7 (TeX 803-807); used in the proof of Corollary 6.16 (TeX 3793)
items.note: The paper writes I_G(ρ) for I_G(ρ|P_J). Quoted from Morris 1993 (paywalled, not re-read). No atlas layer plans Morris's level-zero intertwining; the SmoothRepresentationsPartII proposal has only Moy–Prasad's depth-zero compact-induction and containment statements (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21/24-/26, from MP96 Proposition 6.6 and Theorem 6.11) and the finite cuspidality predicate (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/33), not this theorem.

items.name: o_F-lattice sequence and its period
items.statement: An o_F-lattice sequence in V is a function Λ from ℤ to the set of o_F-lattices in V such that (i) Λ(k) ⊆ Λ(j) for k ≥ j, and (ii) there is a positive integer e = e(Λ|o_F), the o_F-period, with ϖ_F Λ(k) = Λ(k+e) for all k ∈ ℤ. Direct sums of lattice sequences are as in [BK1, §2].
items.note: Only lattices exist: `Submodule.IsLattice` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean:67, an R-submodule that is finitely generated and spans V over A; its docstring mentions the Bruhat–Tits tree of GL₂ as motivation). Searched declaration names in Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 for Hereditary, LatticeChain, LatticeSeq, LatticeFunction, Stratum/Strata, Cayley: only Fraïssé 'Hereditary' (Mathlib/ModelTheory/Fraisse.lean:100), plumbing-graph lattice chain complexes (TauCeti/LowDimTopology/Plumbing/ChainComplex.lean:51), Hahn-embedding strata and Cayley graphs; atlas.json descriptions contain no 'lattice sequence', 'lattice function', 'hereditary order', 'Bushnell', 'Kutzko', 'simple strat', 'semisimple strat'. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans 'the GL_n model from homothety classes of norms/lattice chains', which is the building, not lattice sequences with their filtrations. items.name: Dual lattices and self-dual lattice sequences (normalized d = 1, even period)
items.statement: For an o_F-lattice L, L^# = {v ∈ V : h(v, L) ⊆ p_F}. A lattice sequence Λ is self-dual if there is d ∈ ℤ with Λ(k)^# = Λ(d − k) for all k; all self-dual lattice sequences are normalized so that d = 1 and all periods are even (this changes only the indexing). The orthogonal direct sum of self-dual lattice sequences is self-dual.
items.note: The normalization was checked: if d is odd, Λ′(k) = Λ(k + (d−1)/2) has d = 1; if d is even, Λ′(k) = Λ(⌊k/2⌋ + d/2) has d = 1 and doubled period. Mathlib's `LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean:37, {x | ∀ y ∈ N, B x y ∈ 1}) is the dual into the ring of integers for a bilinear form, not the p_F-dual for a sesquilinear form. No self-dual lattice sequences in either library or the atlas (PELModuli:M1 mentions 'self-dual lattice' levels for abelian schemes, unrelated). Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: The filtration a_n(Λ), the hereditary order a₀(Λ), its radical a₁(Λ), the valuation ν_Λ
items.statement: An o_F-lattice sequence Λ gives a decreasing filtration {a_n(Λ) : n ∈ ℤ} of A by o_F-lattices, a_n(Λ) = {x ∈ A : xΛ(k) ⊆ Λ(k+n) for all k}; a₀(Λ) is a hereditary o_F-order in A and a₁(Λ) is its Jacobson radical; ν_Λ(x) = max{n : x ∈ a_n(Λ)} is a valuation on A with ν_Λ(0) = +∞. If Λ is self-dual then each a_n(Λ) is σ-stable, a_n^-(Λ) = a_n(Λ) ∩ A₋ filters A₋, and ν_Λ is σ-invariant.
items.note: The paper gives the filtration without its formula; the formula above is the standard one of [BK1, §2] (also Kurinczuk–Skodlerack–Stevens, arXiv:1611.02667, 'Lattice sequences and parahoric subgroups'). No hereditary orders in either library (only Fraïssé 'Hereditary'); PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17/hereditary-order is missing and its route was rejected. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: The compact open subgroups P̃(Λ), P̃_n(Λ), P⁺(Λ), P(Λ), P_n(Λ)
items.statement: P̃(Λ) = a₀(Λ)^×, a compact open subgroup of G̃, filtered by the normal subgroups P̃_n(Λ) = 1 + a_n(Λ), n > 0. If Λ is self-dual, P̃ and P̃_n are σ-stable, P⁺(Λ) = P̃(Λ) ∩ G⁺ (compact open in G⁺), P(Λ) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G, and P_n(Λ) = P̃_n(Λ)^Σ = P̃_n(Λ) ∩ G, n > 0, is a filtration of P(Λ) by normal subgroups.
items.locator: §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 8 (TeX 906-913); Introduction p. 2 ('The lattice sequence Λ defines a compact open subgroup P(Λ) in G, together with a filtration')
items.note: P̃_n(Λ)^Σ = P̃_n(Λ) ∩ G⁺ lies in G because det(1 + a_n) ⊆ 1 + p_F contains no −1 (p odd); checked. RG2.3 plans parahoric and congruence group schemes for a general reductive group from root-group charts; the lattice-sequence description of these groups for G̃ and G is not planned. Not in either library. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: The Cayley map a_n^- → P_n(Λ)
items.statement: For n > 0 and Λ self-dual, x ↦ C(x) = (1 + x/2)(1 − x/2)⁻¹ is a bijection a_n^-(Λ) → P_n(Λ), equivariant under conjugation by P(Λ).
items.locator: §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 8 (TeX 913-916); used in §3 (TeX 1446)
items.note: Checked: for x̄ = −x, C(x)‾ = (1 + x/2)⁻¹(1 − x/2) = C(x)⁻¹, so C(x) ∈ G⁺ ∩ (1 + a_n) = P_n; the inverse is g ↦ 2(g − 1)(g + 1)⁻¹, using 2 ∈ o_F^× (p odd). No Cayley transform in either library (only Cayley graphs, Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Cayley.lean). Not planned. Not in Fintzen's branch (which uses a mock exponential, PAPER-FINTZEN-21/16c).

items.name: P(Λ)/P₁(Λ) is a finite reductive group and P°(Λ) is a parahoric subgroup of G
items.statement: For Λ self-dual, 𝒢 = P(Λ)/P₁(Λ) is the group of k₀-points of a reductive group over k₀ = k_{F₀}, not connected in general; P°(Λ), the inverse image in P(Λ) of the k₀-points of the identity component 𝒢°, is a parahoric subgroup of G.
items.note: Asserted without proof or citation (standard; cf. Broussous–Stevens, arXiv:math/0402228, and Morris). Concretely P̃/P̃₁ ≅ ∏_k GL(Λ(k)/Λ(k+1)) over a period, and σ pairs k with −k, so P/P₁ is a product of general linear groups and of the groups of the forms induced on the σ-fixed quotients (indices 0 and e/2), and in the orthogonal case its determinant-one part; this is disconnected in general, as stated. RG2.3 plans connected parahorics and reductive quotients for a general group; the identification of parahorics of classical groups with the P°(Λ) is not planned. Fintzen's branch uses G_{x,0} from RG2.3 (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/29).

items.name: Stratum and equivalence of strata (Definition 2.1(i)-(ii))
items.statement: A stratum in A is a 4-tuple [Λ, n, r, b] with Λ an o_F-lattice sequence, n, r ∈ ℤ, n ≥ r ≥ 0, and b ∈ a_{−n}(Λ). Two strata [Λ, n, r, b_i], i = 1, 2, are equivalent if b₁ − b₂ ∈ a_{−r}(Λ).
items.note: Searched declaration names in Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 for Hereditary, LatticeChain, LatticeSeq, LatticeFunction, Stratum/Strata, Cayley: only Fraïssé 'Hereditary' (Mathlib/ModelTheory/Fraisse.lean:100), plumbing-graph lattice chain complexes (TauCeti/LowDimTopology/Plumbing/ChainComplex.lean:51), Hahn-embedding strata and Cayley graphs; atlas.json descriptions contain no 'lattice sequence', 'lattice function', 'hereditary order', 'Bushnell', 'Kutzko', 'simple strat', 'semisimple strat'. ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) plans the characteristic-zero GL_m(E), E/Q_p finite, 'supercuspidal/type and segment' theory; it does not name strata and does not cover F of characteristic p or the classical-group (skew/self-dual) versions used here. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Skew strata and null strata (Definition 2.1(iii)-(iv))
items.statement: A stratum [Λ, n, r, b] is skew if Λ is self-dual and b ∈ A₋; it is null if n = r and b = 0.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.1(iii)-(iv), arXiv v2 p. 9 (TeX 932-935)
items.note: Later papers call skew strata 'self-dual' strata (Kurinczuk–Skodlerack–Stevens, arXiv:1611.02667, 'Simple strata and concordance', which flags this as a change of terminology). Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Strata as characters: ψ_b on P̃_{r+1}(Λ) and ψ_b^- on P_{r+1}(Λ)
items.statement: For n ≥ r ≥ n/2 > 0, an equivalence class of strata [Λ, n, r, b] corresponds to the character ψ_b : x ↦ ψ_A(b(x − 1)) of P̃_{r+1}(Λ) (trivial on P̃_{n+1}(Λ)), and an equivalence class of skew strata to the character ψ_b^- = ψ_b|_{P_{r+1}(Λ)} of P_{r+1}(Λ).
items.note: Checked that ψ_b is a character: b(x−1)(y−1) ∈ a_{2r+2−n}(Λ) ⊆ a₁(Λ) and ψ_A is trivial on a₁(Λ) (tr_{A/F}(a₁) ⊆ p_F, ψ_F of conductor p_F). Injectivity on classes uses the duality a_k(Λ)* = a_{1−k}(Λ) under (x, y) ↦ ψ_A(xy) ([BK1]); the skew version uses p ≠ 2. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: The critical exponent k₀(β, Λ)
items.statement: For β ∈ A with E = F[β] a field and Λ an o_E-lattice sequence, n_k(β, Λ) = {x ∈ a₀(Λ) : βx − xβ ∈ a_k(Λ)} and k₀(β, Λ) = −∞ if β = 0, and otherwise k₀(β, Λ) = max{ν_Λ(β), sup{k ∈ ℤ : n_k(β, Λ) ⊄ b₀(Λ) + a₁(Λ)}}, where b₀(Λ) = a₀(Λ) ∩ B and B is the centralizer of β. It measures the action of a_β(x) = βx − xβ on the filtration of Λ.
items.locator: §2.1, after Definition 2.2, arXiv v2 p. 9 (TeX 966-969): the paper does not define it and refers to [BK, §1.5] (for lattice chains) and [S1, §5] (for lattice sequences)
items.note: The displayed formula is not in this paper: it is taken from Kurinczuk–Skodlerack–Stevens (arXiv:1611.02667, 'Simple strata and concordance'), which cites [S1, Lemma 5.6] for k₀(β,Λ) = e(Λ|o_F)·k_F(β). A formaliser must take the definition from [BK, (1.4.5)] and [S1, §5]. PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17/critical-exponent is the same notion for GL_n (missing, route rejected). ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) plans the characteristic-zero GL_m(E), E/Q_p finite, 'supercuspidal/type and segment' theory; it does not name strata and does not cover F of characteristic p or the classical-group (skew/self-dual) versions used here.

items.name: Simple stratum (Definition 2.2)
items.statement: A stratum [Λ, n, r, β] in A is simple if either it is null or: (i) E = F[β] is a field; (ii) Λ is an o_E-lattice sequence (Λ is normalized by E^×: each Λ(k) is an o_E-lattice and ϖ_EΛ(k) = Λ(k + e(Λ|o_E)) for all k; printed 'o_E-lattice chain', issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E5), written Λ_{o_E} when so viewed; (iii) ν_Λ(β) = −n; (iv) k₀(β, Λ) < −r.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.2 (cf. [BK, Definition 1.5.5], [BK1, Definition 5.1]), arXiv v2 p. 9 (TeX 952-964)
items.note: Searched declaration names in Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 for Hereditary, LatticeChain, LatticeSeq, LatticeFunction, Stratum/Strata, Cayley: only Fraïssé 'Hereditary' (Mathlib/ModelTheory/Fraisse.lean:100), plumbing-graph lattice chain complexes (TauCeti/LowDimTopology/Plumbing/ChainComplex.lean:51), Hahn-embedding strata and Cayley graphs; atlas.json descriptions contain no 'lattice sequence', 'lattice function', 'hereditary order', 'Bushnell', 'Kutzko', 'simple strat', 'semisimple strat'. ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) plans the characteristic-zero GL_m(E), E/Q_p finite, 'supercuspidal/type and segment' theory; it does not name strata and does not cover F of characteristic p or the classical-group (skew/self-dual) versions used here. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Splitting of a stratum; a basis splitting a stratum (Definition 2.3)
items.statement: Given [Λ, n, r, β] and a decomposition V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i into F-subspaces, put Λ^i(k) = Λ(k) ∩ V^i and β_i = 1^i β 1^i, with 1^i the projection onto V^i with kernel ⊕_{j≠i} V^j. (i) The decomposition is a splitting of the stratum if Λ(k) = ⊕_i Λ^i(k) for all k and β = Σ_i β_i. (ii) A basis {v₁, …, v_N} of V splits the stratum if V = ⊕_i F v_i is a splitting.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.3, arXiv v2 p. 9 (TeX 973-989)
items.note: Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Semisimple stratum (Definition 2.4)
items.statement: A stratum [Λ, n, r, β] in A is semisimple if either it is null or ν_Λ(β) = −n and there is a splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i for it such that (i) for 1 ≤ i ≤ l, [Λ^i, q_i, r, β_i] is a simple or null stratum in A^{ii} = End_F(V^i), where q_i = r if β_i = 0 and q_i = −ν_{Λ^i}(β_i) otherwise; and (ii) for i ≠ j, the stratum [Λ^i ⊕ Λ^j, q, r, β_i + β_j] is not equivalent to a simple or null stratum, where q = max{q_i, q_j}. Block notation: A^{ij} = Hom_F(V^j, V^i), M_β = ⊕_i A^{ii}.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.4 (= [S4, Definition 3.2]), arXiv v2 p. 9 (TeX 992-1009); Introduction p. 2
items.note: The central definition of the local data. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it. ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) plans the characteristic-zero GL_m(E), E/Q_p finite, 'supercuspidal/type and segment' theory; it does not name strata and does not cover F of characteristic p or the classical-group (skew/self-dual) versions used here.

items.name: Uniqueness of the splitting of a semisimple stratum
items.statement: If [Λ, n, r, β] is semisimple, the splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i of Definition 2.4 is uniquely determined, up to ordering, by the stratum.
items.locator: §2.1, after Definition 2.4, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1005-1006)
items.note: Stated without proof (from [S4]). The V^i are the images of the primitive idempotents of F[β] = ⊕ F[β_i], so the splitting is determined by β once F[β] = ⊕ E_i is known. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: E = F[β] = ⊕ E_i, the centralizer B, the groups G̃_E, G̃_{E_i}, the Levi M̃_β, and b_n(Λ)
items.statement: For a semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β] with splitting ⊕ V^i: E = F[β] = ⊕_{i=1}^l E_i with E_i = F[β_i]; 'Λ is an o_E-lattice sequence' means Λ = ⊕ Λ^i with Λ^i an o_{E_i}-lattice sequence in V^i. B = B_β is the A-centralizer of β, B = ⊕ B_i with B_i the centralizer of β_i in A^{ii}; G̃_E = B^×, G̃_i = Aut_F(V^i), G̃_{E_i} = B_i^× = G̃_i ∩ G̃_E; M̃_β = M_β^× is a Levi subgroup of G̃ and G̃_E = ∏ G̃_{E_i} ⊆ M̃_β; each G̃_{E_i} is the F₀-points of the restriction of scalars to F₀ of a general linear group over E_i; b_n(Λ) = a_n(Λ) ∩ B is the filtration of B induced by Λ as an o_E-lattice sequence.
items.note: Centralizers and Levi subgroups of GL_N are elementary; restriction of scalars is planned in ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a. The filtration b_n(Λ) and the o_E-lattice-sequence convention are not in either library or the atlas. Fintzen's twisted Levi subgroups (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/8) are the analogue for tame groups; here E/F may be wildly ramified. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Skew semisimple stratum (Definition 2.5)
items.statement: A semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β] is skew if Λ is self-dual, β ∈ A₋, and the associated splitting V = ⊕ V^i is orthogonal with respect to h.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.5, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1031-1035); Introduction p. 2 ('skew semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β]')
items.note: Introduction p. 2 describes such β as 'an elliptic semisimple element of the Lie algebra of G'; this fails in one edge case (issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E1). Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Structure of skew semisimple strata and of the centralizers G_E⁺ ⊇ G_E
items.statement: Let [Λ, n, r, β] be skew semisimple with splitting ⊕ V^i. Then: (a) each [Λ^i, q_i, r, β_i] is a skew simple stratum for the form h_i induced by h on V^i; (b) the involution of F extends to each E_i as the adjoint involution, with fixed field E_{i,0}, a subfield of index 2 except when E_i = F = F₀ (so β_i = 0); (c) G_E⁺ = B ∩ G⁺ is the F₀-points of a reductive group over F₀ and G_E = B ∩ G the F₀-points of its identity component; G_E⁺ = ∏ G⁺_{E_i}, G_E = ∏ G_{E_i}, each G⁺_{E_i} being the F₀-points of the restriction of scalars to F₀ of a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over E_{i,0}; (d) at most one G⁺_{E_i} is symplectic or orthogonal, and this happens only when β_i = 0 and F = F₀; (e) G_{E_i} = G⁺_{E_i} unless G⁺_{E_i} is orthogonal, in which case G_{E_i} is special orthogonal.
items.locator: §2.1, after Definition 2.5, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1037-1057); Introduction p. 2 ('G_E ... is a product of classical groups over extensions of F₀')
items.note: Stated without proof. Checked (b): if F = F₀ and β_i ≠ 0 then β̄_i = −β_i, so the involution of E_i is nontrivial; and (c),(e): for a unitary factor, det_F g = N_{E_{i,0}/F}(N_{E_i/E_{i,0}}(det_{E_i} g)) = 1, so the condition det = 1 defining SO(V) only cuts down the orthogonal factor. When that factor is SO(1,1)(F) the centre of G_E is not compact (issues PAPER-STEVENS-08/E1, PAPER-STEVENS-08/E2). Not in either library or the atlas. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: [BS, Lemmas 5.2-5.5]: hermitian forms f_i over E_i/E_{i,0} with the same lattice duality
items.statement: For each i there is a nondegenerate E_i/E_{i,0} ε-hermitian form f_i on V^i such that the notions of lattice duality for o_{E_i}-lattices in V^i defined by h_i and by f_i coincide; G⁺_{E_i} is the group of fixed points in G̃_{E_i} of the involution determined by f_i.
items.locator: §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1059-1064), citing Broussous–Stevens, arXiv:math/0402228, Lemmas 5.2-5.5
items.note: Quoted, not re-read (the printed sign is the same ε; with h = λ∘f for an F-linear λ : E_i → F commuting with the involutions the sign is preserved). Used again in §6 (TeX 2658). Not in either library or the atlas. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: The centralizer groups P̃_n(Λ_{o_E}), P_n(Λ_{o_E}), P⁺(Λ_{o_E}), P(Λ_{o_E}), P°(Λ_{o_E})
items.statement: P̃_n(Λ_{o_E}) = P̃_n(Λ) ∩ G̃_E = 1 + b_n(Λ) and P_n(Λ_{o_E}) = P_n(Λ) ∩ G_E (n > 0); P̃(Λ_{o_E}) = P̃(Λ) ∩ G̃_E, P⁺(Λ_{o_E}) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G_E⁺, P(Λ_{o_E}) = P(Λ) ∩ G_E; P°(Λ_{o_E}) is the inverse image in P(Λ_{o_E}) of the identity component of P(Λ_{o_E})/P₁(Λ_{o_E}), a parahoric subgroup of G_E; it can be smaller than P°(Λ) ∩ G_E.
items.locator: §2.1, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1066-1074); Introduction pp. 2-3
items.note: Same status as PAPER-STEVENS-08/20 and PAPER-STEVENS-08/22. The main theorems use P°(Λ_{o_E}) being a maximal parahoric of G_E (PAPER-STEVENS-08/248-PAPER-STEVENS-08/255). Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: [BK, Theorem 1.6.1]: the simple intersection property for GL_N
items.statement: (As used in the proof of Lemma 2.6.) For a simple stratum [Λ, n, 0, β] and x ∈ G̃_E: P̃₁(Λ) x P̃₁(Λ) ∩ G̃_E = P̃₁(Λ_{o_E}) x P̃₁(Λ_{o_E}).
items.locator: §2.1, proof of Lemma 2.6, arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1094-1095)
items.note: Quoted from Bushnell–Kutzko 1993 (not re-read). Only level one is used, and a₁(Λ) is the radical of a₀(Λ) for any lattice sequence, so the chain case applies. Double cosets are Mathlib `DoubleCoset.doubleCoset` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/DoubleCoset.lean:37); the theorem is absent. ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) plans the characteristic-zero GL_m(E), E/Q_p finite, 'supercuspidal/type and segment' theory; it does not name strata and does not cover F of characteristic p or the classical-group (skew/self-dual) versions used here. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: [S1, Lemma 2.1] (as used): fixed points of pro-p double cosets under a group of order prime to p
items.statement: (As applied twice in the proof of Lemma 2.6.) Let Γ be a finite group of automorphisms of G̃ of order prime to p (here a 2-group, p ≠ 2), K a Γ-stable pro-p subgroup and x ∈ G̃ fixed by Γ. Then (K x K) ∩ G̃^Γ = K^Γ x K^Γ. Applications: Γ = the conjugations by Σ ε_i 1^i (ε_i = ±1), with fixed points M̃_β, and Γ = Σ.
items.locator: §2.1, proof of Lemma 2.6, arXiv v2 pp. 10-11 (TeX 1096-1106), citing Stevens, Manuscripta Math. 106 (2001)
items.note: The precise hypotheses of [S1, Lemma 2.1] were not re-read (paper not on arXiv); the statement records the form used. Searched 'Glauberman', 'coprimeAction', fixed points of double cosets: only a Burnside-type count (TauCeti/GroupTheory/DoubleCoset/Orbits.lean:366) and a ramification lemma. Not planned. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Equation (2.7): the semisimple intersection property in G̃
items.statement: Let [Λ, n, 0, β] be a skew semisimple stratum (the argument uses only that it is semisimple). For x ∈ G̃_E: P̃₁(Λ) x P̃₁(Λ) ∩ G̃_E = P̃₁(Λ_{o_E}) x P̃₁(Λ_{o_E}).
items.locator: §2.1, proof of Lemma 2.6, equation (2.7), arXiv v2 p. 10 (TeX 1088-1102); used for the first statement of Lemma 2.6 (TeX 1105-1106)
items.note: Proof checked: [S1, Lemma 2.1] with Γ = {conjugation by Σ ε_i 1^i} (a 2-group preserving P̃₁(Λ) because Λ is split) gives P̃₁xP̃₁ ∩ M̃_β = (P̃₁ ∩ M̃_β) x (P̃₁ ∩ M̃_β) = ∏_i P̃₁(Λ^i) x_i P̃₁(Λ^i), and then [BK, Theorem 1.6.1] in each block (null blocks trivially). Kurinczuk–Stevens (arXiv:1509.02212, 'Semisimple intersection property') generalize it to two lattice sequences. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 (first statement): semisimple intersection property in G⁺
items.statement: Let [Λ, n, 0, β] be a skew semisimple stratum. Then P₁(Λ) x P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E⁺ = P₁(Λ_{o_E}) x P₁(Λ_{o_E}) for all x ∈ G_E⁺.
items.note: Proof checked: take σ-fixed points of (2.7) and apply [S1, Lemma 2.1] with Γ = Σ on both sides; P̃₁(Λ_{o_E})^σ = P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E⁺ = P₁(Λ_{o_E}) because P₁(Λ) ⊆ G. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 (second statement): semisimple intersection property in G
items.statement: Let [Λ, n, 0, β] be a skew semisimple stratum. Then P₁(Λ) x P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E = P₁(Λ_{o_E}) x P₁(Λ_{o_E}) for all x ∈ G_E.
items.note: Follows from PAPER-STEVENS-08/39 by intersecting with G, since P₁(Λ) ⊆ G. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Lattice-function model of the building of G̃ ([BL])
items.statement: There is a G̃-equivariant bijection, unique up to translation, between the (extended) affine building I(G̃, F₀) of G̃ = Aut_F V (= Res_{F/F₀} GL_F(V)) and the set of o_F-lattice functions on V; the lattice sequences correspond to the rational points (barycentres of vertices with rational weights). Points of the building and lattice sequences are identified, so one can speak of the line segment [Λ, Λ′].
items.locator: §2.2, arXiv v2 p. 11 (TeX 1123-1136); Introduction p. 3 ('the description of the building in terms of lattice functions (see [6] or §2.2)')
items.note: RG2.2: 'Construct the GL_n model from homothety classes of norms/lattice chains and identify the SL_2 tree as a validation example', together with the reduced/enlarged comparison (norms are equivalent to lattice functions, Goldman–Iwahori). The lattice-sequence ↔ rational-point dictionary and the translation ambiguity should be part of that model; Broussous–Lemaire (Transform. Groups 7 (2002)) is the source. Not built in either library (no 'building' declarations). Fintzen's branch imports buildings from RG2.2 as well.

items.name: The involution on the building and the building of G⁺ as self-dual lattice functions ([BS])
items.statement: The involution σ of G̃ induces an involution of I(G̃, F₀) which, for a unique choice of the identification of PAPER-STEVENS-08/41, is Λ ↦ Λ^# with Λ^#(k) = (Λ(1 − k))^# on lattice sequences; its fixed-point set is identified with the affine building I(G⁺, F₀). Thus I(G⁺, F₀) is the set of self-dual lattice functions on V, and self-dual lattice functions are identified with points of both I(G⁺, F₀) and I(G̃, F₀).
items.locator: §2.2, arXiv v2 p. 11 (TeX 1127-1136), citing Broussous–Lemaire and Broussous–Stevens (arXiv:math/0402228)
items.note: RG2.2 builds I(G⁺) abstractly by Bruhat–Tits gluing and plans no self-dual lattice-function model and no identification of I(G⁺) with the σ-fixed points of I(G̃) (which uses p ≠ 2). Not in either library. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: The embedding of buildings I(G̃_E, F₀) ↪ I(G̃, F₀)
items.statement: Identifying an o_E-lattice sequence with a point of I(G̃_E, F₀) and of I(G̃, F₀) gives a continuous affine injection j : I(G̃_E, F₀) ↪ I(G̃, F₀) ([BL]); it respects apartments, and I(G̃_E, F₀) ≅ ∏_i I(G̃_{E_i}, F₀) with I(G̃_{E_i}, F₀) ≅ I(B_i^×, E_i). The same holds for self-dual lattice sequences and the buildings of G_E⁺, G⁺.
items.note: The tame analogue, the image of the building of a tame twisted Levi subgroup, is PAPER-FINTZEN-21/8a, routed by an accepted source route to ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2; it covers only tame E/F, while here E/F may be wildly ramified (p odd only), and Fintzen fixes the image, not a canonical map. Record as missing (a request to RG2.2). Not in either library.

items.name: [Sec2, Lemme 1.5(i)]: a neighbourhood on which a₀ decreases
items.statement: (Translated into lattice sequences.) For an o_F-lattice sequence Λ there is a neighbourhood of Λ in I(G̃, F₀) such that a₀(Λ) ⊇ a₀(Λ″) for all Λ″ in it.
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Lemma 2.8, fact (i), arXiv v2 p. 11 (TeX 1152-1155), citing Sécherre, Compositio 141 (2005)
items.note: True: the facets meeting a small neighbourhood of Λ contain the facet of Λ in their closure, then use PAPER-STEVENS-08/46. Building topology and facets are planned in RG2.2, this lemma is not. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: [Sec2, Lemme 1.5(ii)], extended: approximating by lattice sequences with prescribed b₀
items.statement: Given o_E-lattice sequences Λ, Λ′ with b₀(Λ) ⊇ b₀(Λ′), there is a sequence of o_E-lattice sequences Λ_j with b₀(Λ_j) = b₀(Λ′) and lim Λ_j = Λ. In the self-dual case the Λ_j can be taken self-dual (replace Λ_j by the barycentre of Λ_j and Λ_j^#).
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Lemma 2.8, fact (ii) and last paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 11 (TeX 1156-1171)
items.note: [Sec2] gives the simple case; the semisimple case uses I(G̃_E) ≅ ∏ I(B_i^×, E_i) (PAPER-STEVENS-08/43). Checked: b₀(Λ) ⊇ b₀(Λ′) means Λ lies in the closure of the facet of Λ′ in I(G̃_E); rational points of that facet accumulate at Λ; for self-dual Λ′ the facet is σ-stable, and the barycentre of Λ_j and Λ_j^# stays in it and tends to Λ. Not planned. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Order inclusion and facet closure
items.statement: For o_F-lattice sequences Λ, Λ′: a₀(Λ′) ⊇ a₀(Λ) if and only if Λ′ lies in the closure of the facet of I(G̃, F₀) containing Λ. The same holds for b₀ and facets of I(G̃_E, F₀).
items.locator: §2.2, Remark 2.11, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1219-1221); used implicitly in the proofs of Lemmas 2.8, 2.10, 2.12
items.note: RG2.2 plans 'facets, closure order, fixers' and the GL_n lattice model; a₀(Λ)^× = P̃(Λ) is the fixer of the facet of Λ in G̃ = GL_F(V), so this is the GL_n instance of the closure/fixer dictionary. It is not stated as such in RG2.2 and should be recorded as a request. Not in either library.

items.name: Lemma 2.8 (cf. [Sec2, Lemme 1.7])
items.statement: Given (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences Λ, Λ′ with b₀(Λ) ⊇ b₀(Λ′), there is a (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequence Λ″ with b₀(Λ″) = b₀(Λ′) and a₀(Λ) ⊇ a₀(Λ″).
items.note: Proof checked: take Λ″ = Λ_j from PAPER-STEVENS-08/45 for j large, inside the neighbourhood of PAPER-STEVENS-08/44. v1 misprinted a(Λ) for a₀(Λ) in the conclusion; fixed in v2. Not planned; not in Fintzen's branch. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Corollary 2.9: minimal b₀ below a given a₀
items.statement: Given any (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequence Λ, there is a (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequence Λ^m such that b₀(Λ^m) is a minimal (self-dual) o_E-order in B and a₀(Λ^m) ⊆ a₀(Λ).
items.locator: §2.2, Corollary 2.9, arXiv v2 p. 11 (TeX 1175-1180); used in §4 (TeX 1841)
items.note: Follows from Lemma 2.8 applied to Λ and the barycentre Λ′ of a chamber (of the building of G̃_E, resp. G_E⁺) whose closure contains Λ. Not planned. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Remark after Corollary 2.9: the analogue for maximal orders fails
items.statement: Given a (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequence Λ, there need not be a (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequence Λ^M with b₀(Λ^M) a maximal (self-dual) o_E-order in B and a₀(Λ^M) ⊇ a₀(Λ).
items.locator: §2.2, Remark (unnumbered) after Corollary 2.9, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1182-1186); Introduction p. 3 ('unlike the case of GL_n(F), this does not imply ... P(Λ^M) ⊇ P(Λ)')
items.note: Asserted without proof or example; it motivates the path construction of β-extensions in §4. Not planned.

items.name: Lemma 2.10: a path with constant b₀ and nested a₀
items.statement: Let Λ, Λ′ be (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences in V with b₀(Λ) = b₀(Λ′). There is a sequence Λ = Λ₀, Λ₁, …, Λ_t = Λ′ of (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences on the segment [Λ, Λ′] such that, for 1 ≤ i ≤ t: (i) b₀(Λ_i) = b₀(Λ); (ii) a₀(Λ_i) ⊆ a₀(Λ_{i−1}) or a₀(Λ_i) ⊇ a₀(Λ_{i−1}).
items.note: Printed 'lattice sequences in A' for 'in V' (issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E6). Proof correct once 'the points where the segment meets some wall' is read as the walls not containing the segment (issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E9): the segment lies in one facet of I(G̃_E) because b₀(Λ) = b₀(Λ′). Not planned. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Remark 2.11(a): closures of facets are convex
items.statement: If Λ₁, Λ₂, Λ are o_E-lattice sequences with a₀(Λ_i) ⊇ a₀(Λ) for i = 1, 2, then a₀(Λ′) ⊇ a₀(Λ) for every Λ′ on the segment [Λ₁, Λ₂].
items.locator: §2.2, Remark 2.11, first paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1215-1221); used in §3 (TeX 1522)
items.note: By PAPER-STEVENS-08/46 this is the convexity of the closure of a facet; the paper calls it clear. The ingredients (facets, apartments containing two points) are planned in RG2.2; the statement is not. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Remark 2.11(b): stars of points are convex
items.statement: If Λ₁, Λ₂, Λ are o_E-lattice sequences with a₀(Λ_i) ⊆ a₀(Λ) for i = 1, 2, then a₀(Λ′) ⊆ a₀(Λ) for every Λ′ on [Λ₁, Λ₂].
items.locator: §2.2, Remark 2.11, second paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1223-1234)
items.note: Sketch only ('The details are left to the reader'): choose an apartment containing Λ₁, Λ₂ (it then contains Λ) and use the explicit description of a₀ from [BL, Corollary 4.5]. Checked: inside the apartment the set of points whose facet has Λ in its closure is the intersection of the open half-apartments containing Λ for the walls not through Λ, hence convex. Not planned. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Triangles in the building are genuine triangles
items.statement: If Λ, Λ′, Λ″ are (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences with b₀(Λ), b₀(Λ′) ⊆ b₀(Λ″), they lie in a common apartment of I(G̃_E, F₀); since the embedding I(G̃_E, F₀) ↪ I(G̃, F₀) respects apartments, they lie in a common apartment of I(G̃, F₀), so the convex hull [Λ, Λ′, Λ″] is a (possibly degenerate) triangle; likewise in the self-dual case. Notation: [Λ₁, …, Λ_t] is the closed convex hull; for a polygon the Λ_i are distinct and ordered so that the boundary is ∪_{i=1}^t [Λ_i, Λ_{i+1}] with Λ_{t+1} = Λ₁ (printed Λ₀, issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E8).
items.locator: §2.2, paragraphs before and after Lemma 2.12, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1237, 1243)
items.note: Checked: Λ″ lies in the closures of the facets of Λ and Λ′; an apartment containing those two facets contains their closures. Apartments are planned in RG2.2; this is not. Not in Fintzen's branch.

items.name: Lemma 2.12: triangulating a triangle into triangles with nested a₀
items.statement: Let Λ, Λ′, Λ″ be (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences with b₀(Λ) and b₀(Λ′) both contained in b₀(Λ″). Then the triangle [Λ, Λ′, Λ″] is a union of triangles [Λ_i, Λ′_i, Λ″_i], where Λ_i, Λ′_i, Λ″_i are (self-dual) o_E-lattice sequences with a₀(Λ_i) ⊆ a₀(Λ′_i) ⊆ a₀(Λ″_i) (printed 'a₀(Λ_i) ⊂ a_(Λ′_i) ⊂ a₀(Λ″_i)', issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E7).
items.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.12, arXiv v2 p. 12 (TeX 1239-1241; proof TeX 1245-1254); new in v2; used in §2.2 (TeX 1256) and §4 (TeX 2045, 2082)
items.note: Proof checked with the reading of issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E9 (cut by the walls not containing the plane of the triangle): each open cell lies in one facet; with Γ₀ inside a cell, Γ′_i on an open edge and Γ_i a vertex, a₀(Γ₀) ⊆ a₀(Γ′_i) ⊆ a₀(Γ_i) by PAPER-STEVENS-08/46; the vertices are rational, so lattice sequences. Not planned. Not in SmoothRepresentationsPartII as proposed: the Fintzen branch (tame groups, p ∤ |W|) works with Moy–Prasad filtrations and Kim–Yu/Yu data, not with lattice sequences or strata, and the Bushnell–Kutzko GL_n strata/simple-character branch offered by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence) was REJECTED in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17.review.json, so no accepted proposal plans it.

items.name: Addendum to Lemma 2.12: constant b₀ is inherited
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 2.12, if b₀(Λ) = b₀(Λ′) = b₀(Λ″), then also b₀(Λ_i) = b₀(Λ′_i) = b₀(Λ″_i) = b₀(Λ) for every i.
items.locator: §2.2, after Lemma 2.12, arXiv v2 p. 13 (TeX 1256)
items.note: The triangle lies in one facet of I(G̃_E) (a convex set), so every point has the same b₀. Not planned.

items.name: The orders 𝔥(β,Λ) ⊆ 𝔧(β,Λ) and the groups H̃(β,Λ), J̃(β,Λ) with their filtrations (quoted from [S4, §3.2])
items.statement: Hypotheses: F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic, p ≠ 2 (the paper's standing assumption; nothing about h is used), V an N-dimensional F-space, A = End_F V, G̃ = Aut_F V. Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a semisimple stratum in A with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕E_i, B = C_A(E) = ⊕B_i, G̃_E = B^×, P̃(Λ_{o_E}) = P̃(Λ) ∩ G̃_E. Defined inductively along k_0(β,Λ) (S4 §3.2) are o_F-orders 𝔥(β,Λ) ⊆ 𝔧(β,Λ) ⊆ 𝔞_0(Λ); put H̃(β,Λ) = 𝔥(β,Λ)^×, J̃(β,Λ) = 𝔧(β,Λ)^× (compact open subgroups of G̃), filtered by H̃^{m+1}(β,Λ) = H̃(β,Λ) ∩ P̃_{m+1}(Λ) and J̃^{m+1}(β,Λ) = J̃(β,Λ) ∩ P̃_{m+1}(Λ) for m ≥ 0. Moreover J̃(β,Λ) = P̃(Λ_{o_E}) J̃^1(β,Λ).
items.locator: §3.1, running text after 'In [S4, §3.2] we define', arXiv v2 p. 13
items.note: Only recalled here; the inductive definition along k_0 is in [S4] Stevens, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005) §3.2 (simple case BK §3.1). Searched pinned TauCeti and Mathlib (whole-tree grep -rl … | wc -l, 0 files) for hereditary order, lattice chain/sequence, stratum, simple/semisimple character, Bushnell, Kutzko, tame corestriction, parahoric, Moy–Prasad, Iwahori (only the braid Iwahori–Hecke algebra), Bruhat–Tits; atlas stages SR.0–SR.6, RG2.1–RG2.3, ET.6 read: none plans p-adic strata or semisimple characters. ET.6 plans 'supercuspidal/type' theory for GL_m over finite extensions of Q_p only, and does not state BK's 𝔥, 𝔧; the semisimple (non-simple) groups and positive characteristic are outside it. Fintzen's SmoothRepresentationsPartII branch does not cover it: that branch (PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 1) builds Kim–Yu/Yu data for groups split over a tame extension with p ∤ |W| from Moy–Prasad filtrations; it has no lattice-sequence strata, semisimple characters or Bushnell–Kutzko/Stevens Heisenberg representations, and excludes wildly ramified E/F and p | |W| (for Sp_2n or SO_2n+1, p ≤ n), which Stevens allows.

items.name: Skew versions H¹, J¹, J, J⁺ and J°(β,Λ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a skew semisimple stratum (Λ self-dual, β ∈ A₋, orthogonal splitting). Then 𝔥(β,Λ) and 𝔧(β,Λ) are stable under the involution, and one puts J⁺(β,Λ) = J̃(β,Λ) ∩ G⁺, J(β,Λ) = J̃(β,Λ) ∩ G, and likewise H¹(β,Λ) = H̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ G, J¹(β,Λ) = J̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ G, H^{m+1}, J^{m+1}. items.name: Equivalent semisimple stratum with γ in the Levi 𝓜_β at level r = −k_0 ([S4, Proposition 3.4])
items.statement: Hypotheses: F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic, p ≠ 2 (the paper's standing assumption; nothing about h is used), V an N-dimensional F-space, A = End_F V, G̃ = Aut_F V. Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕V^i and put r = −k_0(β,Λ). items.name: Semisimple characters C(Λ,0,β) ([S4, Definition 3.13])
items.statement: Hypotheses: F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic, p ≠ 2 (the paper's standing assumption; nothing about h is used), V an N-dimensional F-space, A = End_F V, G̃ = Aut_F V. Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, M̃_β = 𝓜_β^× the Levi subgroup ∏Aut_F(V^i). C(Λ,0,β) is the set of abelian characters θ̃ of H̃¹(β,Λ) defined inductively along k_0(β,Λ) by: (i) θ̃|_{H̃¹ ∩ M̃_β} = ⊗_{i=1}^l θ̃_i for some simple characters θ̃_i ∈ C(Λ^i,0,β_i) (BK §3.3); (ii) with r = −k_0(β,Λ) and [Λ,n,r,γ] a semisimple stratum equivalent to [Λ,n,r,β] with γ ∈ 𝓜_β (PAPER-STEVENS-08/58), θ̃|_{H̃^{[r/2]+1}(β,Λ)} = θ̃_0|_{H̃^{[r/2]+1}(β,Λ)} · ψ_{β−γ} for some θ̃_0 ∈ C(Λ,0,γ); here ψ_b(x) = ψ_A(b(x−1)), ψ_A = ψ_F∘tr_{A/F}, ψ_F = ψ_0∘tr_{F/F_0}, ψ_0 of conductor 𝔭_0.

items.name: Glauberman description of skew semisimple characters ([S4, §3.6]; this paper §5.3)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. items.name: g-intertwining space I_g(ρ) and intertwining sets I_G(ρ), I_{G⁺}(ρ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. (Used also for two representations ρ of K and ρ' of K', I_G(ρ,ρ') = {g : Hom_{K' ∩ ᵍK}(ρ', ᵍρ) ≠ 0}, e.g. in PAPER-STEVENS-08/68.)

items.name: Remark 3.3: transfer at level m under the corrected condition ⌊m/e⌋ = ⌊m'/e'⌋ (corrects [S4, §3.5])
items.statement: Hypotheses: F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic, p ≠ 2 (the paper's standing assumption; nothing about h is used), V an N-dimensional F-space, A = End_F V, G̃ = Aut_F V. Let [Λ,n,0,β], [Λ',n',0,β] be semisimple strata with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E_i = F[β_i]; for m ≥ 0 let C(Λ,m,β) be the set of restrictions to H̃^{m+1}(β,Λ) of elements of C(Λ,0,β). Put e = e(Λ|o_F)/lcm_{1≤i≤l} e(E_i/F) and e' = e(Λ'|o_F)/lcm_i e(E_i/F). If ⌊m/e⌋ = ⌊m'/e'⌋ (3.4) then ⌊m/e(Λ^i|o_{E_i})⌋ = ⌊m'/e(Λ'^i|o_{E_i})⌋ for every i, and the transfer of [S4, Proposition 3.26] gives a canonical bijection τ : C(Λ,m,β) → C(Λ',m',β) characterized as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/68. The integers m_0, m_0' of [S4, §3.5] satisfy (3.4) because k_0(β,Λ)/e(Λ|o_F) = k_0(β,Λ')/e(Λ'|o_F) (PAPER-STEVENS-08/72).

items.name: Heisenberg lemma underlying Proposition 3.5 (i) (BK Proposition 5.1.1 pattern; implicit via [S4, Corollary 3.29])
items.statement: Let J be a finite p-group (here J¹(β,Λ)/ker θ, a finite quotient of a pro-p group), p odd, H ⊴ J with J/H elementary abelian, and θ a character of H normalized by J such that (xH, yH) ↦ θ([x,y]) is a well-defined nondegenerate alternating pairing J/H × J/H → μ_p. items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. For a skew semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β] (p ≠ 2), the Cayley map x ↦ C(x) = (1 + x/2)(1 − x/2)⁻¹ restricts to bijections 𝔧¹(β,Λ) ∩ A₋ → J¹(β,Λ) and 𝔥¹(β,Λ) ∩ A₋ → H¹(β,Λ), where 𝔧¹ = 𝔧 ∩ 𝔞_1(Λ), 𝔥¹ = 𝔥 ∩ 𝔞_1(Λ).
items.locator: §3.2, proof of Lemma 3.6 ('Since the Cayley map is a bijection…'), arXiv v2 p. 15
items.note: §2.1 states the analogous bijection 𝔞_n^- → P_n(Λ) (chunk A). Searched 'Cayley (transform|map)|cayleyMap': only the complex upper half-plane Cayley map. Fintzen's SmoothRepresentationsPartII branch does not cover it: that branch (PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 1) builds Kim–Yu/Yu data for groups split over a tame extension with p ∤ |W| from Moy–Prasad filtrations; it has no lattice-sequence strata, semisimple characters or Bushnell–Kutzko/Stevens Heisenberg representations, and excludes wildly ramified E/F and p | |W| (for Sp_2n or SO_2n+1, p ≤ n), which Stevens allows.

items.name: Duality: 𝔞_0(Λ) ⊆ 𝔞_0(Λ') implies 𝔞_1(Λ) ⊇ 𝔞_1(Λ')
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. items.name: The configuration Λ^m, Λ, Λ^M, the transferred characters and Heisenberg representations, and the group J¹_{m,M}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. Let [Λ,n,0,β], [Λ^m,n_m,0,β], [Λ^M,n_M,0,β] be skew semisimple strata (necessarily with the same splitting) with 𝔞_0(Λ^m) ⊆ 𝔞_0(Λ) ⊆ 𝔞_0(Λ^M); θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), θ_m = τ_{Λ,Λ^m,β}(θ), θ_M = τ_{Λ,Λ^M,β}(θ); η, η_m, η_M the Heisenberg representations (PAPER-STEVENS-08/73) of J¹, J¹_m = J¹(β,Λ^m), J¹_M = J¹(β,Λ^M) containing θ, θ_m, θ_M. Then J¹_{m,M} := P_1(Λ^m_{o_E}) J¹_M is a group, since P(Λ^M_{o_E}) normalizes J¹_M and contains P_1(Λ^m_{o_E}); and J¹_{m,M} ⊆ P_1(Λ^m).
items.locator: §3.2, setup before Proposition 3.7, arXiv v2 p. 15
items.note: P(Λ^M_{o_E}) ⊆ J(β,Λ^M) normalizes J¹_M by [S4]; P_1(Λ^m_{o_E}) ⊆ 𝔟_0(Λ^m)^× ⊆ 𝔟_0(Λ^M)^×. items.name: Proposition 3.7 (i): existence and uniqueness of η_{m,M}
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. items.name: Quotients J¹_{m,M}/J¹_M and J⁺_M/J¹_M; J¹_{m,M} is a Sylow pro-p subgroup of J⁺_M
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. In the configuration PAPER-STEVENS-08/82 assume moreover 𝔟_0(Λ^m) is a minimal self-dual o_E-order in B. Then J¹_{m,M}/J¹_M ≅ P_1(Λ^m_{o_E})/P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}), a subgroup of J⁺_M/J¹_M ≅ P⁺(Λ^M_{o_E})/P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}) (J⁺_M = J⁺(β,Λ^M)), and J¹_{m,M} is a Sylow pro-p subgroup of J⁺_M.
items.locator: §3.3, first paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 16
items.note: Uses J¹(β,Λ^M) ∩ G_E = P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}) and J⁺ = P⁺(Λ_{o_E})J¹ ([S4]); Sylow because the image is the unipotent radical of a Borel of each connected factor and the component groups have 2-power order. items.name: Structure of P⁺(Λ^M_{o_E})/P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}) = ∏ 𝒢_i and the image 𝒰 of P_1(Λ^m_{o_E})
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. For a skew semisimple stratum with blocks E_i (E_{i,0} the fixed field of the involution on E_i), P⁺(Λ^M_{o_E})/P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}) is identified with ∏_i 𝒢_i, 𝒢_i (the points of) a possibly disconnected reductive group over k_{E_{i,0}}: (a) E_i/E_{i,0} quadratic unramified: a product of restrictions of scalars of general linear groups over k_{E_i} and at most two unitary groups over k_{E_{i,0}}; (b) E_i/E_{i,0} quadratic ramified: a product of general linear groups, at most one symplectic and at most one orthogonal group over k_{E_i} = k_{E_{i,0}}; (c) E_i = F = F_0: a product of general linear groups and at most two symplectic (ε = −1) or orthogonal (ε = +1) groups over k_F. When 𝔟_0(Λ^m) ⊆ 𝔟_0(Λ^M) is a minimal self-dual o_E-order, the image of P_1(Λ^m_{o_E}) is 𝒰 = ∏_i 𝒰_i, 𝒰_i the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup of 𝒢_i.
items.locator: §3.3, list of possibilities, arXiv v2 pp. 16–17
items.note: Stated without proof (standard from the lattice description of parahorics; cf. Morris, Broussous–Stevens). RG2.3 (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3: 'connected reductive quotient of the special fiber' of parahoric group schemes) plans the general connected reductive quotient but not this explicit classical-group/lattice-sequence description nor the disconnected quotient of P⁺; RG2.2 has only the GL_n lattice-chain model. Mathlib/TauCeti have symplecticGroup, star-unitary and orthogonal matrix groups (Mathlib LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean, UnitaryGroup.lean), no finite unitary group of a hermitian form over F_{q²}/F_q.
