items.name: [DM, p. 129]: the derived subgroup of the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a connected reductive group over a finite field k with maximal torus 𝒯 ⊆ Borel ℬ = 𝒯𝒰, root system Σ, positive roots Σ⁺ and simple roots Δ determined by ℬ, root subgroups 𝒰_α (relative roots in the non-split case). Then [𝒰,𝒰] = ∏_{α∈Σ⁺∖Δ} 𝒰_α, except for small-field exceptions (printed: types B_2, F_4 over F_2 and G_2 over F_3; G_2 over F_2 is also an exception, PAPER-STEVENS-08/E15), none of which occurs for classical groups over fields of odd characteristic. Consequently every character of 𝒰 has the form ∏_{α∈Δ} φ_α with φ_α a character of 𝒰_α.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.9, citing [DM] Digne–Michel, Representations of finite groups of Lie type, p. 129; arXiv v2 p. 17
items.note: Only the inclusion ∏_{α∈Σ⁺∖Δ}𝒰_α ⊆ [𝒰,𝒰] is needed. TauCeti has only the opposite inclusion for GL_n: LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/UpperUnitriangular/Nilpotent.lean:220 `theorem commutator_superdiagonalSubgroup_le (r s : ℕ) : ⁅superdiagonalSubgroup r, superdiagonalSubgroup s⁆ ≤ superdiagonalSubgroup (r + s)` (read at pin); no equality, no classical groups. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups Layer 7 plans Borel subgroups and root data of algebraic groups, not this finite-group commutator statement. Finite-group input; Fintzen's branch does not supply it (it needs no Sylow-character analysis of this kind), and it is not SmoothRepresentationsPartII-specific.

items.name: Claim in the proof of Lemma 3.9: characters of 𝒰 intertwined by 𝒢 are trivial except on SL₂(F₃) factors
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be one of the finite groups 𝒢_i of PAPER-STEVENS-08/92 (odd residual characteristic), 𝒰 the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup, and φ a character of 𝒰 intertwined by all of 𝒢 (in fact by the image of the connected component suffices). Write φ = ∏_{α∈Δ}φ_α (PAPER-STEVENS-08/94) and Δ = ⋃Δ_j into irreducible components. (a) If card Δ_j ≥ 2, φ_α is trivial for all α ∈ Δ_j (conjugate by a Weyl representative n with w(α) ∈ Σ⁺∖Δ). (b) If card Δ_j = 1 the factor is GL_2(k_E), SL_2(k_E) = Sp_2(k_E), a unitary group of dimension 2 or 3, or an orthogonal group of dimension 3 or 4; then φ is trivial on that factor (conjugating by diag(a,a⁻¹), resp. diag(a,ā⁻¹) with the norm k_E → k_{E,0} surjective and |k_{E,0}| > 2, diag(a,1,ā⁻¹), diag(a,1,a⁻¹), diag(a,1,1,a⁻¹)), except when the factor is SL_2(F_3), where the two non-trivial characters of 𝒰 ≅ F_3 are intertwined by all of SL_2(F_3).
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.9, cases (i)–(iv), arXiv v2 pp. 17–18
items.note: Checked each case: SL_2 torus acts on 𝒰 by a², so |k| = 3 is the only failure; U(2) root group ≅ k_{E,0} scaled by N(a); U(3): 𝒰/[𝒰,𝒰] ≅ k_E scaled by a; SO_3 and SO_4^± root groups scaled by a. Lemma 3.10 uses this claim with intertwining by G_E only (not G_E⁺); all elements used lie in the connected component, so that is legitimate. TauCeti has GL₂(F_q) character theory (RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/GL2/*) and the GL₂ Borel/Weyl element, but nothing on characters of 𝒰 intertwined by 𝒢 (searched Sylow/unitriangular/GL2Borel files). Finite-group input; Fintzen's branch does not supply it (it needs no Sylow-character analysis of this kind), and it is not SmoothRepresentationsPartII-specific.

items.name: [BK, Proposition 5.2.4] proof (p. 168): the GL₂ case
items.statement: Let k be a finite field with |k| > 2 and 𝒰 the upper unitriangular subgroup of GL_2(k). A character of 𝒰 intertwined by all of GL_2(k) is trivial (conjugation by diag(a,1) scales 𝒰 ≅ k by a).
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.9 case (i), citing [BK, proof of Proposition 5.2.4, bottom of p. 168]; arXiv v2 p. 17
items.note: Statement as used here (BK's text not read). TauCeti has LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Borel.lean `GL2Borel` and the GL₂(F_q) character table layer (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTheory Layer 9), but this intertwining statement is not stated there. Finite-group input; Fintzen's branch does not supply it (it needs no Sylow-character analysis of this kind), and it is not SmoothRepresentationsPartII-specific.

items.name: SL₂(F₃): 𝒰 is a quotient by the normal Sylow 2-subgroup; its characters extend
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = SL_2(F_3) and 𝒰 ≅ F_3 its upper unitriangular subgroup. The non-trivial characters of 𝒰 are intertwined by all of 𝒢; 𝒢 has a normal Sylow 2-subgroup Q (≅ Q_8) with 𝒢 = Q ⋊ 𝒰, so every character of 𝒰 extends to a character of 𝒢 trivial on Q; the extensions of the non-trivial characters are 1-dimensional cuspidal representations of 𝒢.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.9 case (ii), arXiv v2 p. 18
items.note: Checked: 𝒰 ∩ g𝒰g⁻¹ = 1 for g ∉ ℬ and ℬ = {±1}𝒰, so every g intertwines; cuspidal since the restriction to 𝒰 is non-trivial. No atlas stage plans cuspidal representations of SL_2(F_q) (CharacterTheory Layer 9 is GL₂). Finite-group input; Fintzen's branch does not supply it (it needs no Sylow-character analysis of this kind), and it is not SmoothRepresentationsPartII-specific.

items.name: Lemma 3.9: characters of J¹_{m,M}/J¹_M intertwined by J⁺_M extend to J⁺_M

items.name: Self-dual E-basis splitting Λ^m (and Λ^M) with 2×2 normal forms
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. On a hyperbolic plane W carrying an SL_2(k_E) factor of 𝒢_i, after scaling and permuting the basis, 𝔟_0(Λ^m_{o_E})|_W = [[o_E, o_E],[𝔭_E, o_E]] and 𝔟_0(Λ^M_{o_E})|_W = [[o_E,o_E],[o_E,o_E]] or [[o_E,𝔭_E⁻¹],[𝔭_E,o_E]] (the latter when E/E_0 is ramified and the form is hermitian).
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.10, arXiv v2 p. 18
items.note: Checked the two normal forms for E/E_0 ramified: with f(e_1,e_2)=1, o_Ee_1 ⊕ o_Ee_2 gives Sp_2 iff f is skew-hermitian and o_Ee_1 ⊕ 𝔭_Ee_2 (self-dual) gives Sp_2 iff f is hermitian. items.name: Lemma 3.10: a character of J¹_{m,M}/J¹_M intertwined by G_E is trivial
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. items.locator: §3.3, Lemma 3.10 and proof, arXiv v2 p. 18
items.note: Proof: reduce to one block and, by PAPER-STEVENS-08/95, to an SL_2(F_3) factor; take x ∈ P_1(Λ^m_{o_E}) generating that 𝒰 and a torus element g ∈ G_E with gxg⁻¹ ∈ P_1(Λ^M_{o_E}), so φ(x) = φ(gxg⁻¹) = 1. items.name: Two extensions of an irreducible representation differ by a character of the quotient; transfer of intertwining to that character
items.statement: Let G be a group, K ≤ G a subgroup and N ⊴ K (here G = G⁺ of SH, N = J¹_M ⊴ K = J¹_{m,M}), η_N an irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of N and η, η' two extensions of η_N to K. Then η' ≅ η ⊗ φ for a unique character φ of K/N (the character by which K acts on the line Hom_N(η, η')). If g intertwines both η and η' (g ∈ G) and dim I_g(η_N) ≤ 1, then g intertwines φ, i.e. φ = ᵍφ on K ∩ gKg⁻¹.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Corollary 3.11 (implicit), arXiv v2 p. 19
items.note: Checked: I_g(η) and I_g(η') are non-zero subspaces of the line I_g(η_N) (dim 1 by PAPER-STEVENS-08/74), hence equal to it, and comparing the two intertwining relations gives φ = ᵍφ on K ∩ ᵍK. TauCeti has Clifford theory (RepresentationTheory/Induction/Inertia.lean:83 `noncomputable def inertia (A : FDRep k N) : Subgroup G` and Clifford/Equivalence.lean:281 `theorem clifford_restrict_iso … [Field k] [Group G] {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [IsAlgClosed k] (W : FDRep k G) [Simple W]`, read at pin; arbitrary G, finite-dimensional W) and the projective-representation obstruction (ProjectiveRepresentation/*), but not Gallagher's statement (searched 'Gallagher', 'extendib|extends to .*representation|invariant character': no relevant file). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction Layer 7 plans 'V extends iff that class is trivial, and in general the irreducibles of T lying over V are the projective representations of T/N carrying that factor set', of which this is a one-line corollary, but the corollary is not itself stated there. Finite-group input; Fintzen's branch does not supply it (it needs no Sylow-character analysis of this kind), and it is not SmoothRepresentationsPartII-specific.

items.name: Corollary 3.11: uniqueness of η_{m,M} by G_E-intertwining
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residual characteristic p ≠ 2, with a galois involution x↦x̄ of fixed field F_0 (F = F_0 allowed); V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); A = End_F V with adjoint anti-involution a↦ā; G̃ = Aut_F V; σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹ on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A; G⁺ = G̃^σ (a unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group over F_0); G = the F_0-points of the connected component of G⁺ (G = G⁺ except SO ⊂ O in the orthogonal case); A₋ = A^σ; self-dual lattice sequences normalized with Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k) and even period. In the configuration PAPER-STEVENS-08/82, if 𝔟_0(Λ^m) is a minimal self-dual o_E-order contained in 𝔟_0(Λ^M), then η_{m,M} is the unique extension of η_M to J¹_{m,M} which is intertwined by all of G_E.
items.locator: §3.3, Corollary 3.11, arXiv v2 p. 19
items.note: Existence of the G_E-intertwining from PAPER-STEVENS-08/84 (G_E ⊆ J¹_{m,M}G⁺_EJ¹_{m,M}); uniqueness from PAPER-STEVENS-08/101 and Lemma 3.10. v1 stated it without the minimality hypothesis in the statement (it was only in the §3.3 setup); v2 adds it. Used by Miyauchi–Stevens (arXiv 1212.0525, Prop. on η_{Λ,Λ'}) and Kurinczuk–Stevens. items.name: Existence of β-extensions in the maximal case (Theorem 4.1, first part)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). Let [Λ^M,n,0,β] be a skew semisimple stratum such that 𝔟₀(Λ^M) is a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order in B; let θ_M ∈ C₋(Λ^M,0,β) and η_M the unique irreducible representation of J¹_M = J¹(β,Λ^M) containing θ_M. Choose (Cor. 2.9) a self-dual 𝔬_E-lattice sequence Λ^m with 𝔟₀(Λ^m) a minimal self-dual 𝔬_E-order in B and 𝔞₀(Λ^m) ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ^M), and let η_{m,M} be the representation of J¹_{m,M} = P₁(Λ^m_{𝔬_E})J¹_M given by Prop. 3.7 (η_{m,M}|_{J¹_M} = η_M, and η_{m,M}, η_m induce equivalent irreducible representations of P₁(Λ^m)). Then there is a representation κ_M of J⁺_M = J⁺(β,Λ^M) with κ_M|_{J¹_{m,M}} = η_{m,M}.
items.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.1 (cf. [BK, Prop. 5.2.4]), arXiv v2 p. 20; proof p. 20
items.note: Proof read line by line: J⁺_M normalizes η_M, so η_M extends projectively; the class has p-power order (dim η_M a power of p) and dies on the pro-p Sylow J¹_{m,M} (η_M extends there), hence is trivial (items PAPER-STEVENS-08/111–PAPER-STEVENS-08/114); a linear extension λ satisfies λ|_{J¹_{m,M}} = η_{m,M} ⊗ φ with φ a character of P₁(Λ^m_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) intertwined by P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}); Lemma 3.9 extends φ and κ_M = λ ⊗ φ⁻¹. Correct (misprint 'cocycle of J_M' recorded as PAPER-STEVENS-08/E16). items.name: Uniqueness of maximal-case β-extensions up to unipotent-trivial characters (Theorem 4.1, second part)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). In the situation of PAPER-STEVENS-08/107, if κ'_M is another representation of J⁺_M extending η_{m,M}, then κ'_M ≅ κ_M ⊗ χ for some character χ of P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) (inflated to J⁺_M via J⁺_M/J¹_M ≅ P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})) which is trivial on the subgroup generated by all its unipotent subgroups.
items.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.1, last sentence, arXiv v2 p. 20 (proof: 'the final assertion ... is clear')

items.name: Independence of the minimal order: P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) acts transitively on minimal self-dual orders in 𝔟₀(Λ^M)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). Let [Λ^M,n,0,β] be skew semisimple with 𝔟₀(Λ^M) maximal self-dual. Then P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) acts transitively by conjugation on the minimal self-dual 𝔬_E-orders contained in 𝔟₀(Λ^M); since η_{m,M} depends only on 𝔟₀(Λ^m) (Remark after Prop. 3.7) and is transported by this conjugation, the notion of β-extension (PAPER-STEVENS-08/109) does not depend on the choice of Λ^m.
items.locator: §4.1, paragraph after Theorem 4.1, arXiv v2 p. 20
items.note: Stated without proof. Checked: minimal self-dual 𝔬_E-orders inside 𝔟₀(Λ^M) correspond to minimal parabolic (Borel) subgroups of the finite reductive quotient P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}); rational Borels of the connected component are conjugate (Lang), and in the even orthogonal case the two classes of maximal isotropic flags are swapped by O∖SO — this is why P⁺ (not P) is needed. Conjugation by g ∈ P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) ⊆ G⁺_E carries η_{m,M} to η_{gΛ^m,M} because the transfer is characterized by G_E-intertwining (Prop. 3.2). Library: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 7 plans Borel conjugacy geometrically and BN-pairs, but nothing (library or atlas) provides the reductive quotients of self-dual 𝔬_E-orders or rational conjugacy over finite fields. items.name: Sylow extension criterion for normalized representations (used in the proof of Theorem 4.1)
items.statement: Let K be a profinite group, N ⊴ K an open normal subgroup, S ⊆ K a pro-p Sylow subgroup containing N, and η an irreducible smooth complex representation of N of p-power dimension with ᵏη ≅ η for all k ∈ K. If η extends to a representation of S, then η extends to a (linear) representation of K. (Applied with K = J⁺_M, N = J¹_M, S = J¹_{m,M}, η = η_M.)
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1, first paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 20 (after [BK, proof of Prop. 5.2.4] and [Bla, Lemme 6.4])
items.note: Use the relative Clifford class on Q=K/N, not an absolute class on K/ker η. The finite quotient by ker η supplies the pro-p/determinant bridge; it does not change the obstruction quotient. Let N ⊴ K be open pro-p in a profinite group, with invariant irreducible smooth η of finite p-power dimension d. Smoothness and finite dimension make ker η open in N; invariance makes it normal in K, so K/ker η is finite and N/ker η is a finite p-group. Thus m=ord(det η) is a p-power. For the normalized relative lift ρ of item 112 put D(k)=det ρ(k). Since D(nk)=det η(n)D(k), D^m descends to a normalized cochain D̄_m:K/N→ℂˣ. Taking determinants in the factor-set identity yields δD̄_m=α^(dm), so dm[α]=0 on K/N. This is the relative p-primary bound; the bound d[α]=0 alone is generally false there. Restriction to S/N vanishes because η extends to S. The index [K:S] is prime to p, and restriction/corestriction gives [K:S][α]=0; Bézout with the p-power dm forces [α]=0. The relative criterion then supplies a smooth extension of η to K. Components 112–114 and the exact bridge request expose the proof. This repairs the extraction argument and does not refute Stevens’s extension theorem.
proofOutline: Choose a normalized relative projective lift ρ with ρ(1)=1, ρ|N=η, ρ(nk)=η(n)ρ(k), and ρ(k)η(n)ρ(k)⁻¹=η(knk⁻¹). Its factor set in ρ(k)ρ(l)=α(kN,lN)ρ(kl) is a normalized cocycle on Q=K/N with trivial coefficient action. Its class is independent of these choices. It vanishes iff η extends to K: rescale only by a normalized cochain c:Q→ℂˣ, so λ(k)=c(kN)⁻¹ρ(k) preserves η on N. Absolute linearization on K/ker η permits scalar changes on N and is not this criterion.

Let N ⊴ K be open pro-p in a profinite group, with invariant irreducible smooth η of finite p-power dimension d. Smoothness and finite dimension make ker η open in N; invariance makes it normal in K, so K/ker η is finite and N/ker η is a finite p-group. Thus m=ord(det η) is a p-power. For the normalized relative lift ρ of item 112 put D(k)=det ρ(k). Since D(nk)=det η(n)D(k), D^m descends to a normalized cochain D̄_m:K/N→ℂˣ. Taking determinants in the factor-set identity yields δD̄_m=α^(dm), so dm[α]=0 on K/N. This is the relative p-primary bound; the bound d[α]=0 alone is generally false there.

Apply restriction/corestriction on the same relative cohomology carrier: res to S/N is zero, cor∘res=[K:S], and gcd([K:S],dm)=1. The zero relative class gives an extension preserving η, and finite-quotient reduction gives smoothness.

items.name: Relative Clifford obstruction on K/N, preserving the prescribed N-representation
items.statement: Let K be a finite group, N ⊴ K and η an irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of N invariant under K. Equivalently, in the profinite setting use the smooth finite-quotient reduction described in item 111. Choose a normalized relative projective lift ρ with ρ(1)=1, ρ|N=η, ρ(nk)=η(n)ρ(k), and ρ(k)η(n)ρ(k)⁻¹=η(knk⁻¹). Its factor set in ρ(k)ρ(l)=α(kN,lN)ρ(kl) is a normalized cocycle on Q=K/N with trivial coefficient action. Its class is independent of these choices. It vanishes iff η extends to K: rescale only by a normalized cochain c:Q→ℂˣ, so λ(k)=c(kN)⁻¹ρ(k) preserves η on N. Absolute linearization on K/ker η permits scalar changes on N and is not this criterion.
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1 ('we can extend η_M to a projective representation of J⁺_M. This gives rise to a 2-cocycle'), arXiv v2 p. 20
items.note: Import the existing relative Clifford obstruction from Tau Ceti InductionRestriction layer 7, which explicitly places it in H²(T/N,ℂˣ) and characterizes extensions of η. Keep planned status for that actual upstream target. The pinned IsProjectiveRep.cohomologyClass_eq_zero_iff is the absolute linearization ingredient only; it imposes no condition on the scalar cochain restricted to N and cannot replace the relative theorem. The profinite finite-quotient and determinant bridges are explicit requests, not asserted built.
proofOutline: Construct intertwining lifts on the finite quotient; Schur’s lemma gives the relative scalar factor set.

Choose a normalized relative projective lift ρ with ρ(1)=1, ρ|N=η, ρ(nk)=η(n)ρ(k), and ρ(k)η(n)ρ(k)⁻¹=η(knk⁻¹). Its factor set in ρ(k)ρ(l)=α(kN,lN)ρ(kl) is a normalized cocycle on Q=K/N with trivial coefficient action. Its class is independent of these choices. It vanishes iff η extends to K: rescale only by a normalized cochain c:Q→ℂˣ, so λ(k)=c(kN)⁻¹ρ(k) preserves η on N. Absolute linearization on K/ker η permits scalar changes on N and is not this criterion.

items.name: Absolute determinant bound for a finite-dimensional projective representation
items.statement: For a normalized d-dimensional projective representation ρ:Q→GL_d(ℂ), d>0, with ρ(q)ρ(r)=α(q,r)ρ(qr), put D(q)=det ρ(q). Then δD=α^d and d[α]=0 in H²(Q,ℂˣ). This is an absolute statement on the acting group Q; it does not assert d[α]=0 for the relative Clifford class on K/N of a prescribed η.
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1 ('Since the dimension of η_M is a power of p, the order of the cohomology class of this cocycle is a power of p'), arXiv v2 p. 20
items.note: The valid absolute determinant argument is retained separately. In the relative application, det ρ need not descend to K/N; only (det ρ)^m does, for m=ord(det η), giving dm[α]=0. No determinant-one rescaling that changes η|N is permitted. The Heisenberg C₃-centre example has d=1 and relative class of order 3, while its inflated absolute class is zero. The missing exact relative/finite-quotient bridge is requested from the existing InductionRestriction owner; no duplicate projective-representation carrier is proposed.
proofOutline: Take determinants: D(q)D(r)=α(q,r)^d D(qr). Thus α^d is the coboundary of D on Q.
For the relative application use item 111’s m-th determinant power; do not identify Q with K/N until the cochain descends.

items.name: Restriction to a Sylow p-subgroup is injective on the p-primary part of H²
items.statement: For a finite group Q with Sylow p-subgroup S_Q (more generally a profinite group with open subgroup of index prime to p), res: H²(Q, ℂ^×) → H²(S_Q, ℂ^×) is injective on the p-primary component, because cor ∘ res = [Q : S_Q]·id with [Q : S_Q] prime to p. (Used: 'J¹_{m,M} is a Sylow pro-p subgroup of J⁺_M so the original cohomology class of α is trivial'.)
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1, arXiv v2 p. 20
items.note: Library ingredient (read): TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Corestriction.lean:893 `TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitCor2_comp_res2 (x : H2 G M) : explicitCor2 G M U hU (explicitRes2 G M U x) = U.index • x` (continuous H² of a topological group G with a topological G-module M, U open of finite index). The injectivity-on-p-part corollary is not a declaration (grep 'Sylow' in RepresentationTheory/Homological: 0 hits), and Tau Ceti's Schur multiplier (Mathlib groupCohomology.H2) is a different carrier from ContCohomology.H2, so a comparison is also needed. ProfiniteCohomology layer 6 plans cor ∘ res only. Fintzen Part II: not covered. Here the Sylow application must take Q=K/N and S_Q=S/N, with the relative factor-set carrier of item 112. The existing continuous-versus-algebraic carrier comparison remains required; neither the index identity nor the absolute linearization theorem supplies it.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: compatibility of transfer with restriction (commutative diagram)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). Let [Λ,n,0,β], [Λ',n',0,β], [Λ^M,n_M,0,β] be skew semisimple strata with 𝔞₀(Λ) ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ') ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ^M); θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), θ' = τ_{Λ,Λ',β}(θ), θ_M = τ_{Λ,Λ^M,β}(θ); η, η', η_M the corresponding Heisenberg representations. Put J⁺_{Λ,M} = P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ^M) ⊆ J⁺_{Λ',M} = P⁺(Λ'_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ^M) and J⁺_{Λ,Λ'} = P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ'). Then the diagram {ext. of η_M to J⁺_{Λ',M}} →res {ext. of η_M to J⁺_{Λ,M}} → {ext. of η to J⁺(β,Λ)}, {ext. of η_M to J⁺_{Λ',M}} → {ext. of η' to J⁺(β,Λ')} →res {ext. of η' to J⁺_{Λ,Λ'}} → {ext. of η to J⁺(β,Λ)} commutes, the unlabelled maps being the Case-1 bijections of Lemma 4.3.
items.locator: §4.2, Lemma 4.4 (cf. [BK, (5.2.14)]), arXiv v2 p. 21; proof p. 21

Statement says 'semisimple strata' and 'θ' = τ_{Λ,Λ',β}' without argument (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E17). items.name: Definition 4.5: β-extension relative to Λ^M, compatible with κ_M
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕E_i, B = C_A(β), 𝔟_k(Λ) = 𝔞_k(Λ) ∩ B, G̃_E = B^×, G⁺_E = B ∩ G⁺, G_E = B ∩ G; P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G⁺_E, P(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P(Λ) ∩ G_E, P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E, P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) the inverse image of the connected component of P(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}); H̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃(β,Λ) = P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E})J̃¹(β,Λ) the groups of [S4 §3.2]; J⁺ = J̃ ∩ G⁺, J = J̃ ∩ G, J¹ = J̃¹ ∩ G, H¹ = H̃¹ ∩ G, J°(β,Λ) = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ); C(Λ,0,β) the semisimple characters of H̃¹(β,Λ), C₋(Λ,0,β) the skew semisimple characters (restrictions to H¹ of σ-stable ones), τ_{Λ,Λ',β} the transfer (Prop. 3.2); for θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), η = η(θ) is the unique irreducible representation of J¹(β,Λ) containing θ (Prop. 3.5). items.locator: §4.2, Definition 4.5, arXiv v2 p. 23
items.note: Existence of Λ^M: every self-dual 𝔬_E-order lies in a maximal one (implicit). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕E_i, B = C_A(β), 𝔟_k(Λ) = 𝔞_k(Λ) ∩ B, G̃_E = B^×, G⁺_E = B ∩ G⁺, G_E = B ∩ G; P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G⁺_E, P(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P(Λ) ∩ G_E, P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E, P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) the inverse image of the connected component of P(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}); H̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃(β,Λ) = P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E})J̃¹(β,Λ) the groups of [S4 §3.2]; J⁺ = J̃ ∩ G⁺, J = J̃ ∩ G, J¹ = J̃¹ ∩ G, H¹ = H̃¹ ∩ G, J°(β,Λ) = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ); C(Λ,0,β) the semisimple characters of H̃¹(β,Λ), C₋(Λ,0,β) the skew semisimple characters (restrictions to H¹ of σ-stable ones), τ_{Λ,Λ',β} the transfer (Prop. 3.2); for θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), η = η(θ) is the unique irreducible representation of J¹(β,Λ) containing θ (Prop. 3.5). The statements of Lemma 4.3 (PAPER-STEVENS-08/117–PAPER-STEVENS-08/119) hold with P⁺(·) replaced by P°(·) and J⁺ by J°: for 𝔟₀(Λ) ⊇ 𝔟₀(Λ^m) there is a canonical bijection between extensions of η_m to J°(β,Λ^m) and extensions of η to P°(Λ^m_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ), given by equivalence of inductions to P°(Λ^m_{𝔬_E})P₁(Λ^m) when 𝔞₀(Λ) ⊇ 𝔞₀(Λ^m), compatible with restriction from J⁺.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.8 ('using Lemma 4.3 (or rather, its analogue for J°)'; 'together with the analogous Lemma for J°(β,Λ)'), arXiv v2 p. 24
items.note: Asserted without proof. Needs P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ⊆ P°(Λ'_{𝔬_E}) when 𝔞₀(Λ) ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ') (parahoric monotonicity for facets in closures) and the J° version of the Mackey/intersection arguments; plausible. items.name: Proposition 4.8 (i): bijection of β-extensions to J° between two strata
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). Let [Λ,n,0,β], [Λ',n',0,β] be skew semisimple strata such that some skew semisimple [Λ^M,n_M,0,β] has 𝔟₀(Λ^M) a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order containing 𝔟₀(Λ) and 𝔟₀(Λ'); θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), θ' = τ_{Λ,Λ',β}(θ); η, η' the Heisenberg representations. Then there is a canonical bijection between the β-extensions κ' of η' to J°(β,Λ') relative to Λ^M and the β-extensions κ of η to J°(β,Λ) relative to Λ^M.
items.locator: §4.2, Proposition 4.8 (cf. [BK, (5.2.14)]), arXiv v2 p. 24; proof p. 24
items.note: Proof read: reduce (Lemma 2.8 + J° analogue PAPER-STEVENS-08/126) to 𝔞₀(Λ), 𝔞₀(Λ') ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ^M); for 𝔞₀(Λ) ⊆ 𝔞₀(Λ'), Lemma 4.4 + restriction give a well-defined surjection (4.9) between the two finite sets, which have the same cardinality by Lemma 4.10 and Lemma 4.3 (both are in bijection with {κ_M|_{J°_M}}), hence a bijection; general case by composing through Λ^M. Correct. The bijection fails for J⁺ in general, which is why J° is used. items.name: Proposition 4.8 (ii): explicit form and the notion 'compatible'

items.name: Lemma 4.10: restriction to a parabolic-type subgroup detects restriction to J°
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). Let [Λ^M,n_M,0,β] be skew semisimple with 𝔟₀(Λ^M) maximal self-dual containing 𝔟₀(Λ); θ_M ∈ C₋(Λ^M,0,β), η_M its Heisenberg representation, κ_M, κ'_M β-extensions of η_M to J⁺_M. Put J°_M = J°(β,Λ^M) and J°_{Λ,M} = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹_M. Then κ_M|_{J°_{Λ,M}} ≅ κ'_M|_{J°_{Λ,M}} ⟺ κ_M|_{J°_M} ≅ κ'_M|_{J°_M}.
items.locator: §4.2, Lemma 4.10 (inside the proof of Proposition 4.8), arXiv v2 p. 24
items.note: Proof read: κ'_M = κ_M ⊗ χ (Thm 4.1); isomorphism on J°_{Λ,M} forces χ = 1 there (Schur, since the restriction to J¹_M is the irreducible η_M — step left implicit), so χ is trivial on the parabolic 𝒫° of 𝒢° and on unipotent-generated subgroup, hence on 𝒢° (PAPER-STEVENS-08/130). Correct. items.name: A character of a finite reductive group trivial on unipotents and on a parabolic is trivial on the connected component
items.statement: Let 𝒢⁺ = P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) (rational points of a possibly disconnected reductive group over a finite field of odd characteristic) with connected component 𝒢°, and 𝒫° ⊆ 𝒢° a (rational) parabolic subgroup. A character χ of 𝒢⁺ which is trivial on the subgroup generated by all unipotent subgroups and on 𝒫° is trivial on 𝒢°.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.10, arXiv v2 p. 24
items.note: Checked: 𝒢°(k) is generated by B(k) ⊇ T(k) and the rational root subgroups (rational BN-pair of a quasi-split group; Lang's theorem gives quasi-splitness over a finite field). Library: Tau Ceti has abstract Tits systems and the Bruhat decomposition (GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Bruhat/Basic.lean) and a GL₂ instance (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Diagonal/TitsSystem.lean:241 gl2TitsSystem), but no BN-pair for general finite reductive (unitary/symplectic/orthogonal) groups and no Lang theorem; Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 7 plans 'Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems' without rational structure over finite fields. Not planned in the needed form. Fintzen Part II: not covered.

items.name: The image of P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) in 𝒢° = P°(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) is a parabolic subgroup
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). If 𝔟₀(Λ) ⊆ 𝔟₀(Λ^M) (self-dual 𝔬_E-orders), then P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) ⊆ P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ⊆ P°(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) and 𝒫° = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) is a parabolic subgroup of 𝒢°.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.10 ('which is a parabolic subgroup of 𝒢°'), arXiv v2 p. 24
items.note: Stated without proof (standard parahoric/parabolic correspondence for nested facets). RG2.3 plans 'compatibility for nested facets' of parahoric group schemes of connected reductive groups, but the identification of P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) with a parahoric of G_E via self-dual lattice sequences (Broussous–Lemaire/Broussous–Stevens buildings) is not planned anywhere. items.name: Remark: for G̃ = GL_N(F), simple case, β-extensions do not depend on Λ^M; this fails for classical groups
items.statement: For a simple stratum in A = M_N(F), all maximal 𝔬_E-orders in B containing 𝔟₀(Λ) are conjugate under G̃_E, so the set of β-extensions relative to Λ^M is independent of Λ^M. This is no longer true for G⁺ (maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-orders need not be conjugate), but there is a compatibility between β-extensions relative to different maximal self-dual orders (Corollary 6.13, §6).
items.locator: §4.2, unnumbered Remark after Proposition 4.8, arXiv v2 p. 24
items.note: Checked the GL claim: maximal 𝔬_E-orders of B ≅ M_n(E) are all B^×-conjugate to M_n(𝔬_E); independence then follows from BK's intertwining characterization. ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6) plans 'the needed supercuspidal/type and segment theory' for GL_m(E) with E/Q_p finite only (mixed characteristic; its text names no β-extensions, simple characters or Iwahori decompositions); Stevens needs F of any characteristic and semisimple strata, so the item is not planned; the characteristic-0 simple-stratum special case would be imported from ET.6. items.name: The standard maximal self-dual lattice sequence 𝔐_Λ
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕E_i, B = C_A(β), 𝔟_k(Λ) = 𝔞_k(Λ) ∩ B, G̃_E = B^×, G⁺_E = B ∩ G⁺, G_E = B ∩ G; P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G⁺_E, P(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P(Λ) ∩ G_E, P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E, P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) the inverse image of the connected component of P(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}); H̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃(β,Λ) = P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E})J̃¹(β,Λ) the groups of [S4 §3.2]; J⁺ = J̃ ∩ G⁺, J = J̃ ∩ G, J¹ = J̃¹ ∩ G, H¹ = H̃¹ ∩ G, J°(β,Λ) = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ); C(Λ,0,β) the semisimple characters of H̃¹(β,Λ), C₋(Λ,0,β) the skew semisimple characters (restrictions to H¹ of σ-stable ones), τ_{Λ,Λ',β} the transfer (Prop. 3.2); for θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), η = η(θ) is the unique irreducible representation of J¹(β,Λ) containing θ (Prop. 3.5). Write Λ = ⊕_i Λ^i with Λ^i an 𝔬_{E_i}-lattice sequence (normalized self-dual: Λ(k)^# = Λ(1−k)). Define the 𝔬_{E_i}-lattice sequence 𝔐^i_Λ(2r+s) = 𝔭_{E_i}^r Λ^i(s) for r ∈ ℤ, s ∈ {0,1}, and, with e = lcm_i e(E_i/F), 𝔐_Λ(k) = ⊕_i 𝔐^i_Λ(⌈k·e(E_i/F)/e⌉), each block re-indexed to the common 𝔬_F-period 2e (printed as the plain direct sum ⊕_i 𝔐^i_Λ, which is not an 𝔬_F-lattice sequence when the e(E_i/F) differ; PAPER-STEVENS-08/E21). Then [𝔐_Λ,n_𝔐,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum for some n_𝔐, and 𝔟₀(𝔐_Λ) is a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order containing 𝔟₀(Λ).
items.locator: §4.2, display (4.11) and following sentence, arXiv v2 pp. 24–25
items.note: Checked: each 𝔐^i is a self-dual 𝔬_{E_i}-lattice chain {…, Λ^i(0) ⊇ Λ^i(1) ⊇ 𝔭_{E_i}Λ^i(0), …} (Λ^i(1) = Λ^i(0)^# ⊇ 𝔭_{E_i}Λ^i(0)), whose stabilizer order is maximal self-dual and contains 𝔟₀(Λ^i). Literal defect: 𝔐^i has 𝔬_F-period 2e(E_i/F), so for blocks with different ramification indices ⊕_i 𝔐^i is not an 𝔬_F-lattice sequence without re-indexing (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E21); the intended point of the building is clear. Kurinczuk–Stevens 2020 and Miyauchi–Stevens 2014 use the same formula (extended to non-self-dual blocks I_±). items.name: Standard β-extension
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕E_i, B = C_A(β), 𝔟_k(Λ) = 𝔞_k(Λ) ∩ B, G̃_E = B^×, G⁺_E = B ∩ G⁺, G_E = B ∩ G; P⁺(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P⁺(Λ) ∩ G⁺_E, P(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P(Λ) ∩ G_E, P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = P₁(Λ) ∩ G_E, P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) the inverse image of the connected component of P(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}); H̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃¹(β,Λ) ⊆ J̃(β,Λ) = P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E})J̃¹(β,Λ) the groups of [S4 §3.2]; J⁺ = J̃ ∩ G⁺, J = J̃ ∩ G, J¹ = J̃¹ ∩ G, H¹ = H̃¹ ∩ G, J°(β,Λ) = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ); C(Λ,0,β) the semisimple characters of H̃¹(β,Λ), C₋(Λ,0,β) the skew semisimple characters (restrictions to H¹ of σ-stable ones), τ_{Λ,Λ',β} the transfer (Prop. 3.2); for θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), η = η(θ) is the unique irreducible representation of J¹(β,Λ) containing θ (Prop. 3.5). A β-extension of η relative to 𝔐_Λ (PAPER-STEVENS-08/133) is called a standard β-extension (to J⁺(β,Λ), or by restriction to J°(β,Λ)).

items.name: Transfer of standard β-extensions between strata with the same 𝔐_Λ
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). If [Λ,n,0,β], [Λ',n',0,β] are skew semisimple strata with 𝔐_Λ = 𝔐_{Λ'}, θ ∈ C₋(Λ,0,β), θ' = τ_{Λ,Λ',β}(θ), then Proposition 4.8 gives a bijection between the standard β-extensions of η to J°(β,Λ) and those of η' to J°(β,Λ').
items.locator: §4.2, last paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 25
items.note: Immediate from Proposition 4.8 with Λ^M = 𝔐_Λ = 𝔐_{Λ'} (𝔟₀(𝔐_Λ) contains both 𝔟₀'s). items.name: β-extensions for G̃ and semisimple characters (§4.3, stated without proof)
items.statement: For a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β] in A = End_F(V) (G̃ = GL_F(V)) and θ̃ ∈ C(Λ,0,β) with Heisenberg representation η̃ of J̃¹(β,Λ), the constructions of §§4.1–4.2 (using Prop. 3.12 in place of Props. 3.7/3.11) give β-extensions κ̃ of η̃ to J̃(β,Λ); the notion is independent of the choice of Λ^M with 𝔟₀(Λ^M) a maximal 𝔬_E-order containing 𝔟₀(Λ); J̃(β,Λ)/J̃¹(β,Λ) ≅ P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P̃₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) is always connected; and there is a canonical bijection between β-extensions for different Λ as in Proposition 4.8. (Only the simple-character case, from [BK §5.2], is used later.)
items.locator: §4.3, arXiv v2 p. 25
items.note: 'The proofs are identical ... left as an exercise'; the paper states it uses only the simple case (PAPER-STEVENS-08/137). ET.6 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6) plans 'the needed supercuspidal/type and segment theory' for GL_m(E) with E/Q_p finite only (mixed characteristic; its text names no β-extensions, simple characters or Iwahori decompositions); Stevens needs F of any characteristic and semisimple strata, so the item is not planned; the characteristic-0 simple-stratum special case would be imported from ET.6. items.name: [BK §5.2] β-extensions for simple characters of GL_N(F) (literature; as cited by Stevens)
items.statement: Bushnell–Kutzko, The admissible dual of GL(N) via compact open subgroups (1993), §5.2, as cited: for a simple stratum [𝔄,n,0,β] in M_N(F) and a simple character θ with Heisenberg representation η of J¹(β,𝔄), (a) [Prop. 5.2.4] when 𝔅 = 𝔄 ∩ B is maximal, η_{m,M} extends to J(β,𝔄); (b) [Prop. 5.2.5] the induction-equivalence bijection between extensions for nested orders; (c) [(5.2.14)] its compatibility with restriction; (d) [Prop. 5.2.6] a β-extension restricts to η_{m} on the pro-p Sylow; (e) [Remark p. 170] such extensions exist also for non-maximal 𝔅. BK define β-extensions as extensions of η to J(β,𝔄) intertwined by all of G̃_E and prove they exist; Stevens remarks (§4 intro) that BK §5.2 shows the transfer/η_{m,M} characterization used in this paper is equivalent for GL_N(F).
items.locator: Cited in §4 intro, Theorem 4.1, Remark 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Lemma 4.4, Prop. 4.7, Prop. 4.8, §4.3 (arXiv v2 pp. 19–25); used directly for the GL blocks in §4.3 ('when they all come from [BK, §5.2]')

items.name: Decompositions compatible with the splitting, and their idempotents
items.statement: Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a semisimple stratum in A with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i. Consider decompositions V = ⊕_{j=1}^m W^{(j)} such that (i) W^{(j)} = ⊕_i (W^{(j)} ∩ V^i) for all j (so V^i = ⊕_j (W^{(j)} ∩ V^i)), and (ii) each W^{(j)} ∩ V^i is an E_i-subspace of V^i. Let 𝐞^{(j)} be the projection onto W^{(j)} with kernel ⊕_{k≠j} W^{(k)}; M̃ = stabilizer of the decomposition (a Levi subgroup of G̃), 𝓜 its stabilizer in A (M̃ = 𝓜^×), P̃ = M̃Ũ any parabolic with Levi M̃, Ũ_l the unipotent radical of the opposite parabolic.
items.locator: §5.1, opening paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 25
items.note: Conditions (i),(ii) imply 𝐞^{(j)} ∈ B. items.name: Definition 5.1 (i): subordinate decomposition
items.statement: A decomposition V = ⊕_j W^{(j)} as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/139 is subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β] if Λ(r) = ⊕_{j=1}^m (Λ(r) ∩ W^{(j)}) for all r ∈ ℤ (equivalently 𝐞^{(j)} ∈ 𝔞₀(Λ), hence 𝐞^{(j)} ∈ 𝔟₀(Λ)).

items.name: Definition 5.1 (ii): properly subordinate decomposition
items.statement: A decomposition V = ⊕_j W^{(j)} is properly subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β] if it is subordinate and, for all r ∈ ℤ and 1 ≤ i ≤ l, there is at most one j with Λ(r) ∩ W^{(j)} ∩ V^i ⊋ Λ(r+1) ∩ W^{(j)} ∩ V^i.
items.locator: §5.1, Definition 5.1(ii), arXiv v2 p. 25
items.note: Same as BK's 'properly subordinate' in the simple case; Miyauchi–Stevens 2014 quote it verbatim. items.name: Description of (properly) subordinate decompositions via splitting bases
items.statement: Simple case: if 𝓑 is an E-basis of V splitting Λ, any partition 𝓑 = ⊔_j 𝓑_j gives, with W^{(j)} = E-span of 𝓑_j, a subordinate decomposition, and every subordinate decomposition arises so. With e = e(Λ|𝔬_E) and 𝓑_j = {w ∈ 𝓑 : w ∈ Λ(j+re)∖Λ(j+re+1) for some r} (1 ≤ j ≤ e), every coarsening of V = ⊕_{j=1}^e W^{(j)} is properly subordinate, and every properly subordinate decomposition arises so. Semisimple case: taking (properly) subordinate decompositions V^i = ⊕_j W^{(i,j)} of the simple strata [Λ^i,n_i,0,β_i] (some pieces possibly 0) and W^{(j)} = ⊕_i W^{(i,j)} gives a (properly) subordinate decomposition of V.
items.locator: §5.1, explanatory paragraphs after Definition 5.1, arXiv v2 pp. 25–26
items.note: Stated without proof. Checked the properly-subordinate mechanism: a basis vector w with jump index k_w ≡ j (mod e) and its 𝔭_E-multiples jump only at indices ≡ j, so at each r only the block j ≡ r (mod e) jumps. items.name: Iwahori decomposition of a subgroup with respect to (M̃,P̃)
items.statement: A subgroup K ⊆ G̃ has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M̃,P̃) (P̃ = M̃Ũ, Ũ_l the opposite unipotent radical) if K = (K ∩ Ũ_l)(K ∩ M̃)(K ∩ Ũ) (and then the factorization of each element is unique).
items.locator: Used throughout §5 without definition (standard; [BK §7.1], [BH1 §10]), arXiv v2 pp. 26–34
items.note: Not defined in the paper. Mathlib/Tau Ceti: no 'Iwahori' declarations (grep); RG2.4 plans Iwasawa/Cartan/Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions, a different notion. SmoothRepresentationsPartII (Fintzen route 1): only an analogue — Fintzen's branch proves Iwahori-type decompositions/G-covers for Kim–Yu types built from Moy–Prasad groups (tame, p ∤ |W|); it does not supply this lattice-theoretic statement.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (i): H̃¹ and J̃¹ have Iwahori decompositions for subordinate decompositions
items.statement: Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a semisimple stratum in A (G̃ = GL_F(V), F as in the standing hypotheses), V = ⊕_j W^{(j)} a decomposition as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/139 subordinate to it, M̃ its stabilizer and P̃ any parabolic with Levi M̃ and unipotent radical Ũ. Then H̃¹(β,Λ) and J̃¹(β,Λ) have Iwahori decompositions with respect to (M̃,P̃).
items.locator: §5.1, Proposition 5.2(i) (cf. [BK, Thm 7.1.14]), arXiv v2 p. 26
items.note: Proof read: 𝐞^{(j)} ∈ 𝔟₀(Λ); 𝔍¹(β,Λ) (and 𝔥¹) is a 𝔟₀(Λ)-bimodule [S4, Lemma 3.10] (PAPER-STEVENS-08/147), so 𝐞^{(j)}𝔍¹𝐞^{(k)} ⊆ 𝔍¹ and [BH1, Prop. 10.4] (PAPER-STEVENS-08/148) applies. Correct. Kurinczuk–Stevens 2020 cite it for H̃^{m+1}. items.name: Proposition 5.2 (ii): J̃ has an Iwahori decomposition for properly subordinate decompositions, and J̃ ∩ Ũ = J̃¹ ∩ Ũ
items.statement: In the situation of PAPER-STEVENS-08/144, if the decomposition is properly subordinate, then J̃(β,Λ) also has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M̃,P̃), and J̃(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ = J̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ Ũ = P̃₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ Ũ for properly subordinate decompositions
items.statement: In the situation of PAPER-STEVENS-08/145 (properly subordinate), P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ Ũ = P̃₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ Ũ; additively, 𝐞^{(j)}𝔟₀(Λ)𝐞^{(k)} ⊆ 𝔟₁(Λ) for j ≠ k.

items.name: [BH1, Prop. 10.4] Iwahori decomposition criterion for 1 + 𝔍 (literature)
items.statement: Bushnell–Henniart, Local tame lifting for GL(N) I (Publ. IHÉS 83, 1996), Prop. 10.4, as used: if 𝔍 ⊆ 𝔞₁(Λ) is an 𝔬_F-lattice with 1 + 𝔍 a group and 𝐞^{(j)}𝔍𝐞^{(k)} ⊆ 𝔍 for all j,k (idempotents of a decomposition V = ⊕W^{(j)}), then 1 + 𝔍 has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M̃,P̃) for every parabolic P̃ with Levi M̃.

items.name: [BK, Thm 7.1.14 / Lemma 7.1.15] Iwahori decomposition of P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}) (literature; proof reused)
items.statement: Bushnell–Kutzko (1993), Theorem 7.1.14 and Lemma 7.1.15, as used: for a simple stratum and a properly subordinate decomposition, U(𝔅) = P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}) has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M̃,P̃) and U(𝔅) = (U(𝔅) ∩ M̃)U¹(𝔅); Stevens asserts the same proof works for semisimple strata given Lemma 5.3.
items.locator: §5.1, proof of Proposition 5.2(ii), arXiv v2 p. 27
items.note: BK not re-read; the semisimple extension is asserted ('the same proof'). items.name: Restricted strata [Λ^{(j)},n^{(j)},0,β^{(j)}]
items.statement: For a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β] and a subordinate decomposition V = ⊕_j W^{(j)}: Λ^{(j)}(r) = Λ(r) ∩ W^{(j)}, β^{(j)} = 𝐞^{(j)}β𝐞^{(j)}, A^{(j)} = End_F(W^{(j)}), B^{(j)} = C_{A^{(j)}}(β^{(j)}). Claim: [Λ^{(j)},n^{(j)},0,β^{(j)}] is a semisimple stratum in A^{(j)} for some n^{(j)}, with splitting W^{(j)} = ⊕_i (V^i ∩ W^{(j)}) (zero pieces omitted).
items.locator: §5.1, paragraph before Proposition 5.4, arXiv v2 p. 27
items.note: Claim stated without proof ('since each V^i ∩ W^{(j)} is an E_i-subspace'). Note k₀(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}) may be smaller than k₀(β,Λ) when W^{(j)} misses blocks (relevant to PAPER-STEVENS-08/151, PAPER-STEVENS-08/157; see C/N2). items.name: Proposition 5.4 (i): H̃¹ ∩ M̃ and J̃¹ ∩ M̃ are products over the blocks
items.statement: Let [Λ,n,0,β] be semisimple and V = ⊕_j W^{(j)} subordinate, M̃ its stabilizer. Then H̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ M̃ = ∏_{j=1}^m H̃¹(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}) and J̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ M̃ = ∏_{j=1}^m J̃¹(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}) (additively 𝐞^{(j)}𝔥(β,Λ)𝐞^{(j)} = 𝔥(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}), likewise for 𝔍).
items.locator: §5.1, Proposition 5.4, arXiv v2 p. 27; proof pp. 27–28
items.note: Proof read: induction on k₀; choose 𝔬_{E_i}-bases splitting Λ^{(i,j)} to get a generalized (W,E)-decomposition V^i = Y^i ⊗_F E_i [BK1 §5.3] and, by [S4, Prop. 3.4], γ ∈ ∏_i ι_{Y^i}(End_F(E_i)) ⊆ 𝓜 with [Λ,n,r,γ] ~ [Λ,n,r,β]; then 𝐞𝔥(β)𝐞 = 𝔟₀(Λ^{(j)}) + 𝔥^{[r/2]+1}(γ^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}) = 𝔥(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}). The last equality when k₀ drops on the block is not argued but holds (C/N2). items.name: [S4, Prop. 3.4] approximation of a semisimple stratum by one with γ in a prescribed embedded algebra (literature)
items.statement: Stevens (Duke 2005), Prop. 3.4, as used: given a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β], r = −k₀(β,Λ), and generalized (W,E)-decompositions V^i = Y^i ⊗_F E_i adapted to Λ, there is a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,r,γ] equivalent to [Λ,n,r,β] with γ in the image of ∏_i ι_{Y^i}: ∏_i End_F(E_i) ↪ ⊕_i A^{ii}.
items.locator: §5.1, proof of Proposition 5.4, arXiv v2 p. 27 (also recalled in §3.1 in the weaker form γ ∈ 𝓜_β)
items.note: Not re-read; the stronger form (γ in the image of the chosen ι_{Y^i}) is what the proof needs — formalizers must check that S4 Prop. 3.4 provides it. items.name: [BK1 §5.3] generalized (W,E)-decomposition and the embedding ι_Y (literature)
items.statement: Bushnell–Kutzko, Semisimple types (Compositio 119, 1999), §5.3, as used: an F-subspace Y ⊆ V^i with V^i = Y ⊗_F E_i (spanned by an E_i-basis splitting the lattice sequence) gives an algebra embedding ι_Y: End_F(E_i) ↪ End_F(V^i) acting on the E_i-factor; when Y = ⊕_j Y^{(i,j)} is compatible with W^{(i,j)} = Y^{(i,j)} ⊗ E_i, its image lies in A^{ii} ∩ 𝓜.
items.locator: §5.1, proof of Proposition 5.4, arXiv v2 p. 27
items.note: Not re-read. Tau Ceti has tensor products and extension of scalars but no (W,E)-decomposition/ι_Y. items.name: The groups H̃¹_P̃, J̃¹_P̃, J̃_P̃
items.statement: For a semisimple stratum, a subordinate decomposition with stabilizer M̃ and a parabolic P̃ = M̃Ũ: H̃¹_P̃ = H̃¹(β,Λ)(J̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ), J̃¹_P̃ = H̃¹(β,Λ)(J̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ P̃), and, when properly subordinate, J̃_P̃ = H̃¹(β,Λ)(J̃(β,Λ) ∩ P̃). Claim: all these groups have Iwahori decompositions with respect to any parabolic subgroup with Levi component M̃.
items.locator: §5.1, last paragraph, arXiv v2 p. 28
items.note: These are groups because H̃¹ is normal in J̃. Iwahori claim unproved; follows as in BK §7.2 from Prop. 5.2 and the multiplicativity of block decompositions. Lemma 5.8 uses J̃_P̃ also when only subordinate (C/N1). items.name: Proposition 5.5 (i): θ̃ is trivial on H̃¹ ∩ Ũ
items.statement: Let [Λ,n,0,β] be semisimple, V = ⊕_j W^{(j)} subordinate, P̃ = M̃Ũ any parabolic with Levi M̃, and θ̃ ∈ C(Λ,0,β). Then θ̃|_{H̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ} is trivial.
items.locator: §5.2, Proposition 5.5 (cf. [BK, Prop. 7.1.19]), arXiv v2 p. 28; proof pp. 28–29
items.note: Proof read: by [S4, Lemma 3.15(i)] θ̃ is trivial on H̃¹ ∩ Ũ_β for parabolics with Levi M̃_β; using the Iwahori decomposition of H̃¹ ∩ Ũ relative to (M̃_β,P̃_β) one reduces to H̃¹ ∩ Ũ ∩ M̃_β, handled block by block by the simple case [BK1, Prop. 5.2]. items.name: Proposition 5.5 (ii): Iwahori factorization of semisimple characters
items.statement: In the situation of PAPER-STEVENS-08/156, identifying H̃¹(β,Λ) ∩ M̃ = ∏_j H̃¹(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}) (Prop. 5.4), θ̃|_{H̃¹ ∩ M̃} = ⊗_{j=1}^m θ̃^{(j)} with θ̃^{(j)} ∈ C(Λ^{(j)},0,β^{(j)}).
items.locator: §5.2, Proposition 5.5, arXiv v2 p. 28; proof p. 29
items.note: Proof read: θ̃^{(j)} := θ̃|_{H̃¹(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)})} satisfies the two characterizing properties (S4 Def. 3.13): (i) its block restrictions are the simple characters τ_{Λ^i,Λ^{(i,j)},β_i}(θ̃_i) [BK1 §5]; (ii) ψ_{β−γ} restricts to ψ_{β^{(j)}−γ^{(j)}} and induction. Printed 'level 0' for the equivalence of [Λ^{(j)},…,γ^{(j)}] and [Λ^{(j)},…,β^{(j)}] should be level r (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E23). items.name: Finite Heisenberg representation theory used in Corollary 5.7 (Stone–von Neumann with isotropic induction)
items.statement: Let Q be a finite p-group (p odd) with a normal subgroup Z ⊇ [Q,Q], Q/Z elementary abelian, and a character θ of Z normalized by Q such that (x,y) ↦ θ[x,y] is a nondegenerate alternating form on the 𝔽_p-space Q/Z. Then there is a unique irreducible representation η of Q containing θ, dim η = (Q:Z)^{1/2}; and if Q/Z = W₀ ⊥ (W₋ ⊕ W₊) with W_± totally isotropic, dual to each other and orthogonal to W₀, then, given a subgroup U₊ ⊆ Q with U₊Z/Z = W₊ and θ trivial on U₊ ∩ Z, the group Q_P = preimage of W₀ ⊕ W₊ carries a unique irreducible η_P containing the character θ_P of ZU₊ (θ_P(zu) = θ(z)), η ≅ Ind_{Q_P}^Q η_P, and η_P is the space of U₊-fixed vectors of η.
items.locator: §5.2, Corollary 5.7 and remark after Lemma 5.8 (via [BK §7.2]); §3.2 Prop. 3.5 via [S4, Cor. 3.29], arXiv v2 pp. 30–31
items.note: Mathlib/Tau Ceti: no Heisenberg group or Stone–von Neumann (grep 'Heisenberg', 'Stone' hits unrelated). Atlas: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–MP.1 plan Heisenberg groups and Stone–von Neumann only over characteristic-0 local fields (per the accepted FINTZEN-21 review); the finite case with polarization/parabolic fixed vectors is the accepted FiniteWeilRepresentationsPartII proposal (FINTZEN-21 route 3: 'finite Stone–von Neumann uniqueness ... For V = V⁺⊕V⁰⊕V⁻, identify the V⁺-invariant model ... iterated isotropic fixed-vector consequence'), a proposal, not a stage — hence missing. That proposal would cover exactly this finite core (coordinate with it rather than rebuilding).

items.name: The refined decomposition (5.9) and the Iwahori lattice sequence Λ^m
items.statement: Choose E_i-bases 𝓑_{i,j} of W^{(i,j)} = V^i ∩ W^{(j)} splitting Λ^{(i,j)}; the decomposition V = ⊕_{i,j} ⊕_{v∈𝓑_{i,j}} E_i v (5.9) is subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β] and refines both V = ⊕W^{(j)} and the splitting. With M̃₀ its stabilizer, P̃₀ ⊆ P̃ a parabolic with Levi M̃₀ (Ũ₀ ⊇ Ũ) and 𝒫₀ = Lie(P̃₀): 𝒫₀ ∩ 𝔟₀(Λ) + 𝔟₁(Λ) is a minimal 𝔬_E-order 𝔟₀(Λ^m); [Λ^m,n_m,0,β] is semisimple, (5.9) is subordinate to it, P̃(Λ^m_{𝔬_E}) is an Iwahori subgroup of G̃_E contained in P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}), and P̃(Λ^m_{𝔬_E}) = (P̃(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ P̃₀)P̃₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ⊆ H̃¹(β,Λ)(J̃(β,Λ) ∩ P̃) (which is J̃_P̃ when the decomposition is properly subordinate; the paper writes J̃_P̃ here), and that group normalizes θ̃_P̃.
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Lemma 5.8, display (5.9) and following, arXiv v2 p. 30

items.name: Self-dual decomposition
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). A decomposition V = ⊕_{j=−m}^m W^{(j)} is self-dual if for all j the orthogonal complement of W^{(j)} is ⊕_{k≠−j} W^{(k)} (W^{(0)} = {0} allowed). Its stabilizer M̃ is σ-stable; one takes P̃ a σ-stable parabolic with Levi M̃, M⁺ = M̃ ∩ G⁺, P⁺ = P̃ ∩ G⁺, M = M̃ ∩ G, P = P̃ ∩ G, U = Ũ ∩ G.

items.name: Corollary 5.10 (i): Iwahori decompositions of H¹, J¹ in G
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). items.name: Glauberman correspondence for σ-stable pro-p groups (literature, as recalled from [S2 §2])
items.statement: Let K̃ be a σ-stable pro-p subgroup of G̃ (p odd, σ of order 2) and K = K̃^σ. σ acts on representations by ρ̃^σ(k) = ρ̃(k^σ). There is a bijection ρ̃ ↦ ρ = 𝐠(ρ̃) between equivalence classes of σ-stable irreducible representations of K̃ and irreducible representations of K; it commutes with irreducible restriction and irreducible induction; 𝐠(ρ̃) is the unique component of ρ̃|_K occurring with odd multiplicity; if ρ̃ is a character then 𝐠(ρ̃) = ρ̃|_K.
items.locator: §5.3, paragraph 'Let K̃ be a σ-stable pro-p subgroup', arXiv v2 p. 32 (details referred to [S2, §2] = Stevens PLMS 2001; originally Glauberman 1968)

items.name: Lemma 5.12 (i)–(ii): uniqueness of η_P and η ≅ Ind η_P
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (paper §2.1): F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with residue characteristic p ≠ 2, with a (possibly trivial) involution of fixed field F₀; V an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h; A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹; G⁺ = G̃^σ the unitary, symplectic or orthogonal group, G its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO). η_P is the unique irreducible representation of J¹_P whose restriction to H¹_P contains θ_P, and η ≅ Ind_{J¹_P}^{J¹(β,Λ)} η_P.

items.name: Mackey restriction formula and induction in stages (tool used in Lemma 4.4, Cor. 5.7, Prop. 5.13)
items.statement: For subgroups H, K of a group G and a representation A of H: Res_K Ind_H^G A ≅ ⊕_{KsH ∈ K∖G/H} Ind_{K ∩ sHs⁻¹}^K Res(ˢA); and Ind_H^G ∘ Ind_L^H ≅ Ind_L^G. (Applied to open subgroups of compact groups and smooth finite-dimensional representations, i.e. finite-index situations.)
items.locator: §4.2 proof of Lemma 4.4 ('only one double coset in the Mackey restriction formula'); §5.3 before Prop. 5.13; arXiv v2 pp. 21, 33

Mathlib's Rep.ind is k[G] ⊗_{k[H]} A, which is the (compact) induction and agrees with Ind for finite index. Smooth-category versions: SR.2 plans Mackey filtrations for smooth induction.

items.name: Mackey irreducibility criterion (tool for 'induce equivalent irreducible representations')
items.statement: For a finite group G, H ≤ G and a finite-dimensional complex representation A of H: Ind_H^G A is irreducible iff A is irreducible and, for every s ∉ H, Hom_{H ∩ sHs⁻¹}(A, ˢA) = 0.
items.locator: Implicit in Lemma 4.3 (irreducibility of the inductions to P⁺(Λ^m_{𝔬_E})P₁(Λ^m)), Prop. 4.8 and Cor. 5.7; arXiv v2 pp. 21–30

items.name: The pair (K_P, λ_P) attached to λ = κ|_K ⊗ ρ
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E = F[β] = ⊕ E_i, B the A-centralizer of β, G⁺_E = B ∩ G⁺, G_E = B ∩ G, 𝔟_r(Λ) = 𝔞_r(Λ) ∩ B; θ ∈ 𝒞₋(Λ,0,β) is a skew semisimple character, η the unique irreducible representation of J¹(β,Λ) containing θ, and κ a β-extension of η to J⁺(β,Λ) relative to some Λ^M (𝔟₀(Λ^M) a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order containing 𝔟₀(Λ)). V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is a self-dual decomposition properly subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β]; M⁺ is its stabilizer in G⁺, P⁺ = M⁺U a parabolic subgroup of G⁺ with Levi M⁺ and unipotent radical U, U_l the unipotent radical of the opposite parabolic, M = M⁺ ∩ G, P = P⁺ ∩ G; H¹_P, J¹_P, J⁺_P, J°_P, the representations η_P (of J¹_P) and κ_P (of J⁺_P, on the (J¹(β,Λ) ∩ U)-fixed vectors of κ) are as in §5.3, with κ_P|_{J⁺(β,Λ)∩M⁺} = κ^{(0)} ⊗ ⊗_{j=1}^m κ̃^{(j)}, κ^{(0)} an extension of η^{(0)} to J⁺(β^{(0)},Λ^{(0)}) and κ̃^{(j)} an extension of η̃^{(j)} to J̃(β^{(j)},Λ^{(j)}). Let K be a compact open subgroup of G⁺ (printed: 'of G'; see issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E31) with J¹(β,Λ) ⊆ K ⊆ J⁺(β,Λ) having an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M⁺,P⁺), with K ∩ M⁺ = K^{(0)} × ∏_{j=1}^m K̃^{(j)}. Let ρ be the inflation to K of an irreducible representation of K/J¹(β,Λ) and λ = κ|_K ⊗ ρ. Put K_P = H¹(β,Λ)(K ∩ P⁺) and let λ_P be the natural representation of K_P on the space of (J¹(β,Λ) ∩ U)-fixed vectors of λ.

items.name: [BK, Proposition 4.1.3 and Corollary 4.1.5]: Hecke algebra of an induced representation
items.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group (in [BK], GL_N(F); the argument is general), K' ⊆ K compact open subgroups, λ' a smooth finite-dimensional (irreducible) representation of K' and λ = Ind_{K'}^{K} λ'. Then c-Ind_K^G λ ≃ c-Ind_{K'}^G λ' gives a canonical algebra isomorphism H(G,λ') ≅ H(G,λ) (4.1.3); under it, a function in H(G,λ) supported on a single double coset K y K corresponds to a function in H(G,λ') supported on a union of (K',K')-double cosets contained in K y K (4.1.5). Used with K' = K_P, λ' = λ_P.
items.locator: Quoted in the proof of Lemma 6.1(iv), §6.1, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 35; [BK] = Bushnell–Kutzko, The admissible dual of GL(N) via compact open subgroups, Ann. of Math. Stud. 129 (1993), §4.1
items.note: General smooth-representation fact (transitivity of compact induction plus Frobenius reciprocity), stated here as Stevens uses it; the BK book was not re-read for this job. Needs PAPER-STEVENS-08/9 and compact induction (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2 plans 'compact induction … Frobenius reciprocity … induction in stages', not Hecke algebras of representations). Not in either library (searched Hecke algebra: Mathlib 2 files (HeckeRing/Defs.lean, FLT/Basic.lean docstring), Tau Ceti 2 files (HeckeRing/GLn, GL2 diamond cosets), all scalar classical Hecke operators). Belongs with the general type/Hecke-algebra layer of SmoothRepresentationsPartII (Fintzen /1b presupposes ρ-spherical algebras but lists no such isomorphism).

items.name: Definition 6.5: exactly subordinate decomposition
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a skew semisimple stratum. A self-dual decomposition V = ⊕_{j=-m}^m W^{(j)} is exactly subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β] if it is minimal amongst all self-dual decompositions properly subordinate to [Λ,n,0,β], i.e. no refinement of it is properly subordinate to the stratum. items.name: Characterization of exactly subordinate decompositions by maximal orders
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). A decomposition properly subordinate to the skew semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β] is exactly subordinate iff 𝔞₀(Λ^{(0)}) ∩ B^{(0)} is a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order in B^{(0)} and, for each j ≠ 0, there is i with W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i and 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} a maximal 𝔬_{E_i}-order in B^{(j)}. In particular Proposition 6.3 applies to all blocks of an exactly subordinate decomposition.
items.locator: §6.1, paragraph after Definition 6.5, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 37
items.note: Stated without proof; consistent with the printed Definition 6.5 (a block W^{(j)} meeting two V^i, or with two jump classes, can be split keeping proper subordination). It does NOT imply that P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ M is a maximal parahoric of G_E ∩ M: checked example — G = SO_{2n}(F) split, β = 0, Λ the self-dual chain {M ⊂ M^*} with M = L₀ ∩ L₁ for the two adjacent hyperspecial lattices L₀ = ⟨e_i,f_i⟩, L₁ = ⟨ϖ⁻¹e₁, ϖf₁, e_i, f_i (i ≥ 2)⟩ (M^*/M a split hyperbolic plane): 𝔟₀(Λ) is maximal self-dual, the trivial decomposition is the only properly subordinate one (e₁ and f₁ jump at the same index), but P°(Λ) (reductive quotient SO₂ × SO_{2n−2} with SO₂ ≅ GL₁ split) lies in P(L₀), so is not maximal (issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E27). items.name: The invariants i_j, q_j(Λ), ν(j) and the standard numbering of blocks
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum and V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is a self-dual decomposition subordinate (not necessarily exactly subordinate) to it such that, for every j ≠ 0, W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i for some i = i_j and 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} is a maximal 𝔬_{E_i}-order in B^{(j)} = End_{E_i}(W^{(j)}); the numbering is the one fixed in §6.2 (q_j ≥ 0 for j > 0, blocks j > 0 ordered lexicographically by ν(j) = (i_j, q_j)). For j ≠ 0 let i = i_j be the index with W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i and e_i = e(Λ^i|𝔬_{E_i}). Since 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} is maximal there is a unique integer q_j = q_j(Λ) with (i) −e_i/2 ≤ q_j ≤ e_i/2; (ii) Λ(q_j) ∩ W^{(j)} ⊋ Λ(q_j+1) ∩ W^{(j)}; (iii) q_j > −e_i/2 if j > 0 and q_j < e_i/2 if j < 0. By duality i_{−j} = i_j and q_{−j} = −q_j. Renumbering W^{(j)} ↔ W^{(−j)} one assumes q_j ≥ 0 for j > 0, sets ν(j) = (i_j, q_j) ∈ ℤ², and orders the blocks j > 0 lexicographically by ν(j) (ties in either order; j < 0 by duality); the ordering depends on a chosen ordering of the V^i.

items.note: Checked: with lattice sequences normalized so Λ(r)^# = Λ(1−r), a jump of Λ^{(j)} at q gives a jump of Λ^{(−j)} at −q, so q_{−j} = −q_j. items.name: The bases 𝓑^{(±j)}, 𝓑^{(i,0)} and the matrix units I_{j,k}
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum and V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is a self-dual decomposition subordinate (not necessarily exactly subordinate) to it such that, for every j ≠ 0, W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i for some i = i_j and 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} is a maximal 𝔬_{E_i}-order in B^{(j)} = End_{E_i}(W^{(j)}); the numbering is the one fixed in §6.2 (q_j ≥ 0 for j > 0, blocks j > 0 ordered lexicographically by ν(j) = (i_j, q_j)). For j > 0 (i = i_j) choose an ordered 𝔬_{E_i}-basis 𝓑^{(j)} = {v_{j,1},…,v_{j,d_j}} of Λ^{(j)}(0) splitting Λ^{(j)}; then 𝓑^{(j)} ⊆ Λ^{(j)}(q_j) ∖ Λ^{(j)}(q_j+1). With f_i the nondegenerate ε-hermitian E_i/E_{i,0}-form on V^i whose lattice duality agrees with that of h, and ϖ_i a fixed uniformizer of E_i with ϖ̄_i = (−1)^{e(E_i/E_{i,0})−1} ϖ_i, let 𝓑^{(−j)} = {v_{−j,1},…,v_{−j,d_j}} be the ordered basis of W^{(−j)} (printed 'of W^{(j)}', issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E28) with f_i(v_{j,s}, v_{−j,t}) = ϖ_i δ_{st}; it is an 𝔬_{E_i}-basis of Λ^{(−j)}(1) splitting Λ^{(−j)}, and 𝓑^{(−j)} ⊆ Λ^{(−j)}(e_i − q_j) ∖ Λ^{(−j)}(e_i − q_j + 1). For each i choose a (possibly empty) self-dual E_i-basis 𝓑^{(i,0)} of W^{(i,0)} = W^{(0)} ∩ V^i splitting Λ^{(i,0)}. For j,k ≠ 0 with i_j = i_k = i and dim_{E_i}W^{(j)} = dim_{E_i}W^{(k)}, I_{j,k} ∈ B^i is the element sending the ordered basis 𝓑^{(k)} to 𝓑^{(j)} and all other basis vectors to 0 (I_{j,j} = 𝐞^{(j)}, the projection on W^{(j)}).
items.note: Checked the level claims: Λ^{(j)}(0) = Λ^{(j)}(q_j) because the previous jump is at q_j − e_i < 0; the f_i-dual of Λ^{(j)}(0) in W^{(−j)} is Λ^{(−j)}(1) = ⟨𝓑^{(−j)}⟩, which equals Λ^{(−j)}(e_i − q_j) since Λ^{(−j)} jumps at −q_j and e_i − q_j. items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum and V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is a self-dual decomposition subordinate (not necessarily exactly subordinate) to it such that, for every j ≠ 0, W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i for some i = i_j and 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} is a maximal 𝔬_{E_i}-order in B^{(j)} = End_{E_i}(W^{(j)}); the numbering is the one fixed in §6.2 (q_j ≥ 0 for j > 0, blocks j > 0 ordered lexicographically by ν(j) = (i_j, q_j)). With Λ^M as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/224, blocks W^{(j)}, W^{(k)} (j,k ≠ 0) are companion with respect to Λ^M if both lie in the same V^i, dim_{E_i}W^{(j)} = dim_{E_i}W^{(k)}, and for all r ∈ ℤ: Λ^M(r) ∩ W^{(j)} = Λ^M(r+1) ∩ W^{(j)} ⟺ Λ^M(r) ∩ W^{(k)} = Λ^M(r+1) ∩ W^{(k)}. Equivalently i_j = i_k = i, equal dimensions and q_j(Λ^M) ≡ q_k(Λ^M) (mod e_i^M), e_i^M = e(Λ^{M,i}|𝔬_{E_i}).

items.name: Maximal self-dual Λ^{M,i}: jump pattern and q_j(Λ^M) ∈ {0, e_i^M/2}
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). [Λ,n,0,β] is a skew semisimple stratum and V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is a self-dual decomposition subordinate (not necessarily exactly subordinate) to it such that, for every j ≠ 0, W^{(j)} ⊆ V^i for some i = i_j and 𝔞₀(Λ^{(j)}) ∩ B^{(j)} is a maximal 𝔬_{E_i}-order in B^{(j)} = End_{E_i}(W^{(j)}); the numbering is the one fixed in §6.2 (q_j ≥ 0 for j > 0, blocks j > 0 ordered lexicographically by ν(j) = (i_j, q_j)). Suppose 𝔟₀(Λ^{M,i}) is a maximal self-dual 𝔬_{E_i}-order for a fixed i (normalization Λ^M(r)^# = Λ^M(1−r)). Then Λ^{M,i}(0) ⊇ Λ^{M,i}(1) = ⋯ = Λ^{M,i}(e_i^M/2) ⊇ Λ^{M,i}(e_i^M/2 + 1) = ⋯ = Λ^{M,i}(e_i^M) (the lattices are the E_i-multiples of Λ^M(0) ∩ V^i and Λ^M(1) ∩ V^i). Hence for j > 0 with i_j = i: q_j(Λ^M) ∈ {0, e_i^M/2}, W^{(j)} and W^{(−j)} are companion w.r.t. Λ^M, s_j^ϖ ∈ P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) ⟺ q_j(Λ^M) = 0 and s_j ∈ P⁺(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) ⟺ q_j(Λ^M) = e_i^M/2. (The converse fails: if exactly one inclusion is proper the order is maximal, but if both are proper it can be the 'Siegel' order.)

items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). The self-dual decomposition V = ⊕_{j=-m}^{m} W^{(j)} is exactly subordinate (Definition 6.5) to the skew semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β], numbered as in §6.2; M is its stabilizer in G and P = MU a parabolic subgroup of G with Levi component M. Given one σ_j-stable κ̃^{(j)}, the σ_j-stable 2β^{(j)}-extensions are exactly κ̃^{(j)} ⊗ χ̃ ∘ det^{(j)}, where det^{(j)} : End_{E_i}(W^{(j)}) → E_i is the determinant and χ̃ is the inflation of a σ_i-invariant character of k_{E_i}^×, σ_i(x) = x̄^{−1} with x ↦ x̄ the Galois involution of k_{E_i} over k_{E_{i,0}}. If E_i/E_{i,0} is ramified there are two such characters (trivial and quadratic); if E_i/E_{i,0} is unramified there are |k_{E_{i,0}}| + 1. (CORRECTION, issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E33: if E_i = E_{i,0} = F = F₀, i.e. β_i = 0 in a symplectic/orthogonal component, there are two.)

Claimed: (a) if P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) is a maximal parahoric subgroup of G_E then the decomposition is V = W^{(0)}, M = P = G, and N_Λ ⊆ P(Λ_{𝔬_E}) = N_{G_E}(P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})); (b) otherwise, Morris's Levi 𝔐_J (§1) equals M ∩ G_E, 𝔐_J ∩ P_J = P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ M, and N_Λ = N_N(𝔐_J ∩ P_J). CORRECTED (Miyauchi–Stevens 2014): valid when G_E has compact centre and P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) ∩ M is a maximal parahoric subgroup of G_E ∩ M (corrected Definition 6.5); as printed, (a) fails when G_E has a split SO(1,1)(F) factor (normalizer of the parahoric not compact: chunk A issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E1) and (b) fails for the SO_{2n} example of PAPER-STEVENS-08/213 (issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E27).

items.name: [BK, Proposition 5.3.2] technique: intertwiners of κ ⊗ ρ factor as S ⊗ T
items.statement: Let J¹ ◁ J be compact open subgroups, κ a representation of J with κ|_{J¹} = η irreducible, ρ a finite-dimensional representation of J trivial on J¹, and g with dim I_g(η) = 1 (I_g(η) = Hom_{J¹ ∩ ᵍJ¹}(η, ᵍη)). items.name: Cuspidality for a possibly disconnected finite reductive quotient
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a possibly disconnected reductive algebraic group over a finite field k₀, Q=𝒢(k₀) and Q°=𝒢°(k₀), where 𝒢° is its identity component. An irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation τ of Q is cuspidal in Stevens’s convention iff Res_{Q°}τ contains an irreducible cuspidal representation ρ of Q°. Import the connected predicate of PAPER-FINTZEN-21/33 (also Stevens item 10): ρ has no nonzero invariants under U(k₀) for the unipotent radical of any proper k₀-parabolic of 𝒢°. Apply this to P(Λ_{o_E})/P₁(Λ_{o_E}) with connected subgroup P°(Λ_{o_E})/P₁(Λ_{o_E}); the maximal self-dual-order quotient J_M/J¹_M is a specialization, not a separate definition.
items.locator: §6.4, convention before Definition 6.17, arXiv v2 p.43; maximal-order specialization in Proposition 6.18 and consumers in Lemma 7.4 and §§7.2–7.3, pp.43–53
items.note: One shared disconnected convention, importing the connected predicate already identified in item 10 and PAPER-FINTZEN-21/33. Item 306 is merged here, retaining both general/exhaustion and maximal-order consumers. No second finite-reductive cuspidality carrier or roadmap is proposed.

mergedFrom.name: Cuspidal representation of a (possibly disconnected) finite reductive group

For the possibly disconnected 𝒢=P(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}), an irreducible representation is called cuspidal if its restriction to the connected component 𝒢° contains a cuspidal representation.

specializations.name: Maximal self-dual-order quotient
specializations.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). J°_M = P°(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) J¹_M.

items.name: Definition 6.17: maximal simple type (corrected: cuspidal type)
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). The pair (J_M, λ_M) is called a maximal simple type for G. Independent check of the necessity of the maximal-parahoric condition (supports PAPER-STEVENS-08/E2, whose counterexample is SO(1,1)): G = SO_{2n}(F) split (n ≥ 2), β = 0, Λ the self-dual chain {M ⊂ M^*} with M = L₀ ∩ L₁, L₀ = ⟨e_i,f_i⟩, L₁ = ⟨ϖ^{−1}e₁, ϖf₁, e_i, f_i (i ≥ 2)⟩ (adjacent hyperspecial lattices).
