items.name: Clifford's theorem: restriction of an irreducible representation to a normal subgroup
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, G a group, N ◁ G and W an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of G. Then there is an irreducible constituent V of W|_N with inertia group I(V) = {g : ^gV ≅ V} of finite index and e ≥ 1 such that W|_N ≅ e · ⊕_{g ∈ G/I(V)} ^gV. Used with G = J_M (acting through a finite quotient), N = J°_M, W = λ_M (and for τ on P(Λ^M)/P₁ ⊇ P°(Λ^M)/P₁), giving λ_M|_{J°_M} ≅ m ⊕_{p ∈ P(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/N(ρ)} (κ_M ⊗ ρ)^p.
items.locator: Invoked ('by Clifford Theory') in the proof of Proposition 6.18, §6.4, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 43
items.note: Read at the pin: `FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G] {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [IsAlgClosed k] (W : FDRep k G) [Simple W] : ∃ (V : FDRep k N) (_ : Simple V) (hfinite : Finite (G ⧸ inertia V)), ∃ e : ℕ, e ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty (resFDRep N W ≅ V.cliffordSum e)` (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/Clifford/Equivalence.lean:281), with `FDRep.cliffordSum V e` = the FDRep of (q : G ⧸ inertia V) → Fin e → conjNormalFDRep (Quotient.out q) V (Equivalence.lean:67) and dimension form `FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank` (Clifford/Dimension.lean:67); no finiteness of G is assumed, so it applies to the abstract group J_M. The extra step (κ_M ⊗ ρ)^p ≅ κ_M ⊗ ρ^p uses only that κ_M is a representation of J_M ∋ p. Same declarations were credited in PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17/clifford-*.

items.name: [C, Proposition 1.5]: intertwining equal to J implies irreducible compact induction
items.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group (here the classical group G) and J an open subgroup compact modulo the centre, λ an irreducible smooth (finite-dimensional) representation of J with I_G(λ|J) = J. Then c-Ind_J^G λ is irreducible (and, being compactly induced from a compact-mod-centre subgroup, it is supercuspidal: its matrix coefficients are compactly supported modulo the centre).
items.locator: Quoted for Corollary 6.19, §6.4, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 43; [C] = H. Carayol, Représentations cuspidales du groupe linéaire, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 17 (1984), Proposition 1.5
items.note: Planned ingredients only: compact induction and Frobenius reciprocity (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2) and 'matrix-coefficient criteria for supercuspidality' (SR.3); the irreducibility criterion itself is in no stage text. Tau Ceti's finite-group Mackey criterion `TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_iff` (RepresentationTheory/Induction/Mackey/Irreducible.lean:249; [Finite G] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]) is the finite analogue and does not apply to c-Ind from an open subgroup of a non-compact group. In the SmoothRepresentationsPartII proposal the criterion is used implicitly by PAPER-FINTZEN-21/25 (Yu's compact induction irreducible supercuspidal) and /25a (MP96 Prop. 6.6) but is not a separate item; it should be one general layer there.

items.name: [BK2, Proposition 5.4]: an irreducible supercuspidal c-Ind_J^G λ makes (J,λ) a [G,π]_G-type
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive p-adic group, J a compact open subgroup and λ an irreducible smooth representation of J such that π = c-Ind_J^G λ is irreducible (hence supercuspidal). Then (J,λ) is a type for the inertial class [G,π]_G: an irreducible smooth representation of G contains λ iff it is an unramified twist of π (for G with compact centre, iff it is ≅ π).
items.locator: Quoted for Corollary 6.19, §6.4, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 43; [BK2] = Bushnell–Kutzko, Smooth representations of reductive p-adic groups: structure theory via types, Proc. LMS 77 (1998), Proposition 5.4
items.note: The notion of s-type is PAPER-FINTZEN-21/1a (missing, owned by the SmoothRepresentationsPartII proposal, general reductive G) and inertial classes/Bernstein blocks are planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3 ('Construct the Bernstein decomposition'). This specific proposition (supercuspidal case) is not listed in the Fintzen branch; it belongs with its /1a–/1b type layer. No library hits for 'type' in this sense.

items.name: Corollary 6.19: supercuspidal representations of p-adic classical groups by compact induction
items.statement: F is a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic whose residual characteristic p is odd, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution x ↦ x̄ with fixed field F₀; V is an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form h (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), G⁺ = U(V,h) is the full isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal) and G = the F₀-points of its connected component (G = G⁺ except in the orthogonal case, where G = SO(V,h)). Let (J_M, λ_M) be a maximal simple type in G — CORRECTED (Miyauchi–Stevens 2014): a cuspidal type, i.e. with G_E of compact centre and P°(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) a maximal parahoric subgroup of G_E. Then π = c-Ind_{J_M}^G λ_M is an irreducible supercuspidal representation of G and (J_M, λ_M) is a [G,π]_G-type.
items.locator: §6.4, Corollary 6.19, arXiv:math/0607622v2 p. 44 (with the sentence before Definition 6.17, p. 43)
items.note: Stated with the corrected hypotheses (Miyauchi–Stevens 2014, arXiv:1212.0525v1 §3; this is chunk A's issue PAPER-STEVENS-08/E2 — 'Corollary 6.19 as printed is false' — and is not re-recorded at the §6 locator). Deduced from Proposition 6.18 with [C, Prop. 1.5] (PAPER-STEVENS-08/250) and [BK2, Prop. 5.4] (PAPER-STEVENS-08/251). As printed it fails for G = SO(1,1)(F) (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E2) and also for the SO_{2n} edge-midpoint chain recorded in PAPER-STEVENS-08/247's note (G_E of compact centre, 𝔟₀ maximal self-dual, P(Λ^M) maximal compact, P° not a maximal parahoric), which confirms that the maximal-parahoric half of the correction is needed. The sentence before Definition 6.17 ('In the case when P(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) is a maximal compact subgroup of G_E we can now obtain supercuspidal representations') fails for the same example. Exhaustion (every irreducible supercuspidal arises this way) is Theorem 7.14 (chunk E). Overlap with the Fintzen branch of SmoothRepresentationsPartII: PAPER-FINTZEN-21/25 and /5 construct/exhaust supercuspidals of tame G with p ∤ |W| by Yu's construction; classical groups over F with p odd are tame, but p ∤ |W| excludes small odd p (e.g. Sp_{2n} needs p > n), and Yu data are not Stevens's types. So Stevens's odd-p statement is not covered. Previously requested as PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24/38-stevens (missing, route rejected because unread). Searched the pinned trees (Mathlib 082e2d3 at leanenv/TauCeti/.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib and Tau Ceti f790474 at leanenv/TauCeti/TauCeti), case-insensitive, full-tree (no truncation): supercuspidal (0/0 files), parahoric (0/0), Iwahori (1 Tau Ceti hit, KnotTheory Iwahori–Hecke relation only), Bruhat–Tits (0 Tau Ceti; 1 Mathlib, unrelated), Moy (0/0), lattice sequence (0/0), hereditary order (0/0), stratum (8 Tau Ceti files, all Sard/measure-theory strata), semisimple character (0/0), β-extension/beta-extension (0/0), Heisenberg (0/0), Glauberman (0/0), intertwining operator (0/0), distinguished double coset (0/0).

items.name: Compact induction c-Ind_J^G and Frobenius reciprocity
items.statement: For G locally profinite (here G, G⁺ or G̃ with their p-adic topology), J an open subgroup and λ a smooth representation of J, c-Ind_J^G λ is the space of functions f : G → λ with f(jg) = λ(j)f(g), compactly supported modulo J, with G acting by right translation; Frobenius reciprocity Hom_G(c-Ind_J^G λ, π) ≅ Hom_J(λ, π|_J) for J open. Consequently, if c-Ind_J^G λ is irreducible and an irreducible π contains λ, then π ≅ c-Ind_J^G λ (used in §7.3).
items.locator: Used in §1 (H(ρ|K) = End_G(c-Ind_K^G ρ)) and Corollary 6.19, arXiv:math/0607622v2 pp. 7, 44; §7.3, arXiv v2 p. 53
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2 reads: 'Construct smooth induction from closed subgroups and compact induction with support compact modulo the subgroup. Prove Frobenius reciprocity with correct adjoint direction and hypotheses, induction in stages and Mackey filtrations.' Same classification as PAPER-FINTZEN-21/28b. Not in the libraries (searched 'compact induction', 'compactInduction', 'cInd' (19 Mathlib files, all substrings of unrelated identifiers such as snocInduction and AlgebraicIndependent), 'indCompact'). The review merged the duplicate item numbered 304 into this one.

items.name: Supercuspidal representation of G
items.statement: An irreducible smooth complex representation π of the p-adic group G (here the classical group G, a connected reductive group over F₀) is supercuspidal if all its proper Jacquet modules vanish, equivalently its matrix coefficients are compactly supported modulo the centre.
items.locator: Used in Corollary 6.19 and the title of §6, arXiv:math/0607622v2 pp. 34, 44
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2 ('For P=MN define … N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors') and SR.3 ('matrix-coefficient criteria for supercuspidality and temperedness, and the subquotient description by supercuspidal support'). Same as PAPER-FINTZEN-21/28c. 'supercuspidal' has 0 hits in both pinned trees.

items.name: Exhaustion: every supercuspidal of G is induced from a cuspidal (maximal simple) type (Theorem 7.14, corrected)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. Assume moreover that G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group, i.e. not (F=F₀, ε=+1, N=2, h isotropic), when G≅SO(1,1)(F)≅F^× [correction PAPER-STEVENS-08/E3]. Let π be an irreducible supercuspidal representation of G. Then there are a skew semisimple stratum [Λ^M,n,0,β] such that G_E has compact centre and P°(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) is a maximal parahoric subgroup of G_E (conditions of Miyauchi–Stevens 2014, arXiv:1212.0525v1 §3.3 (published: Appendix A), which strengthen Definition 6.17's requirement that 𝔟₀(Λ^M) be a maximal self-dual 𝔬_E-order), a skew semisimple character θ_M∈𝒞₋(Λ^M,0,β) with Heisenberg representation η_M, a β-extension κ_M of η_M to J_M=J(β,Λ^M), and an irreducible representation τ of J_M/J¹_M≅P(Λ^M_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ^M_{𝔬_E}) whose restriction to the connected component contains a cuspidal representation, such that, with λ_M=κ_M⊗τ (a maximal simple type in the sense of Definition 6.17), π≅c-Ind_{J_M}^G λ_M. Corollary (remark after the theorem): every irreducible supercuspidal representation of G is irreducibly compactly induced from a compact open subgroup (the 'folklore conjecture' for G). As printed, the theorem omits the SO(1,1) exclusion (false there, PAPER-STEVENS-08/E3) and its proof uses hypothesis (H), which must be replaced by 'P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) is not a maximal parahoric of G_E or G_E has non-compact centre' (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E4); the §7-local gaps are PAPER-STEVENS-08/E36 and PAPER-STEVENS-08/E37.

No atlas stage plans it: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.3 plan the smooth category, compact induction and supercuspidal support only; ET.6 plans characteristic-0 GL_m(E) type/segment theory, not classical groups. Part II coverage: Fintzen's exhaustion theorem (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/5, Theorem 8.1) covers classical G only when p ∤ |W| (absolute Weyl group orders 2ⁿn! for Sp_{2n}, SO_{2n+1}, 2ⁿ⁻¹n! for SO_{2n}, N! for U_N, so essentially p>n, resp. p>N); classical groups split over an at most quadratic, hence tame, extension since p is odd. Fintzen's conclusion is via Yu's construction, not Stevens's maximal simple types. Stevens's theorem for all odd p (including p | |W|) is not covered. Both allow F of positive characteristic. Route: SmoothRepresentationsPartII, classical-group branch. The paper disclaims unicity (no intertwining-implies-conjugacy for maximal simple types; §7 opening, p. 44).

items.name: The groups J°_{Λ,Λ′} and the representation ϑ′=κ′|⊗ρ (§7.1 set-up)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. [Λ,n,0,β] a skew semisimple stratum with splitting V=⊕_{i=1}^l V^i, E=F[β]=⊕E_i, B=End_E(V), G_E=B∩G=∏G_{E_i}; θ∈𝒞₋(Λ,0,β) a skew semisimple character, η the unique irreducible representation of J¹=J¹(β,Λ) containing θ; J°=J°(β,Λ)=P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹; 𝒢°=J°/J¹≅∏_i P°(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}})/P₁(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}}). Let [Λ′,n′,0,β] be another skew semisimple stratum with 𝔟₀(Λ)⊆𝔟₀(Λ′), θ′=τ_{Λ,Λ′,β}(θ) the transfer, and κ, κ′ compatible β-extensions (Proposition 4.8: relative to a common Λ^M with 𝔟₀(Λ^M) maximal self-dual containing both 𝔟₀'s) to J°(β,Λ), J°(β,Λ′). Let ρ=⊗_iρ_i be the inflation of an irreducible representation of 𝒢°, and ϑ=κ⊗ρ. Put J°_{Λ,Λ′}=P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})J¹(β,Λ′). Then J°_{Λ,Λ′}/J¹(β,Λ′)≅P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ′_{𝔬_E}), which has P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ_{𝔬_E}) as a quotient, so ρ is a representation of J°_{Λ,Λ′}; define the irreducible representation ϑ′=(κ′|_{J°_{Λ,Λ′}})⊗ρ of J°_{Λ,Λ′}.

items.name: Support-preserving Hecke algebra isomorphism H(G,ϑ)≅H(G,ϑ′) (Proposition 7.1)

items.name: The ρ-spherical Hecke algebra H(G,ρ), support, and extension by zero
items.statement: For a locally profinite group G (here G, G_E or a compact open subgroup), a compact open K and an irreducible smooth (finite-dimensional) representation ρ of K: H(G,ρ) is the convolution algebra of compactly supported f:G→End_ℂ(ρ^∨) with f(kgk′)=ρ^∨(k)f(g)ρ^∨(k′) (k,k′∈K), isomorphic to End_G(c-Ind_K^G ρ); its support is a union of K-double cosets contained in the intertwining I_G(ρ). For an open subgroup K′⊇K, extension by zero is an injective algebra map H(K′,ρ)↪H(G,ρ) preserving supports.

items.name: Minimal pair and the factorization ϑ=κ⊗ρ (§7.2 set-up)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. Let π be an irreducible representation of G such that π|_{H¹(β,Λ)} contains some θ∈𝒞₋(Λ,0,β), [Λ,n,0,β] skew semisimple. Fixing β, choose such a pair with 𝔟₀(Λ)=𝔞₀(Λ)∩B minimal. Then π contains the Heisenberg representation η of J¹(β,Λ) (the unique irreducible representation containing θ), hence an irreducible representation ϑ of J°(β,Λ) containing η, and ϑ≅κ⊗ρ with κ a standard β-extension of η (relative to 𝔐_Λ of (4.11)) and ρ=⊗_iρ_i the inflation of an irreducible representation ρ̄=⊗ρ̄_i of 𝒢°=J°/J¹≅∏_i P°(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}})/P₁(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}}) (each 𝒢°_i a connected finite reductive group).

items.name: Gallagher-type factorization for an extension of an irreducible normal-subgroup representation
items.statement: Let N⊴H be groups with H/N finite (in the application N=J¹(β,Λ), H=J°(β,Λ), acting through a finite quotient), η an irreducible representation of N which extends to a representation κ of H. Then every irreducible representation of H whose restriction to N contains η is κ⊗ρ for a unique (up to isomorphism) irreducible representation ρ of H/N, namely ρ=Hom_N(κ,ϑ); conversely each κ⊗ρ is irreducible.
items.locator: Used in §7.2, first paragraph ('Since η extends to J°, we see that ϑ=κ⊗ρ'), and in §7.3, arXiv v2 pp. 46, 53
items.note: Tau Ceti has Clifford theory for restriction to a normal subgroup (FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/Clifford/Equivalence.lean:281: an irreducible W of G restricts to N as e copies of the conjugates of one simple V) but not the Gallagher tensor bijection for an extendible η; Mathlib has nothing (its only 'Gallagher' is the ergodic theorem, Mathlib/NumberTheory/WellApproximable.lean). Part II: Fintzen's extraction of the depth-zero tensor factor (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/23c) uses the same Hom-space argument inside that route; no generic finite-group item is planned. items.name: Minimality forces cuspidal level-zero part (Lemma 7.4)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. In the situation of PAPER-STEVENS-08/264 (𝔟₀(Λ) minimal for fixed β among skew semisimple pairs with π⊇θ), every ρ̄_i is a cuspidal representation of the finite reductive group 𝒢°_i=P°(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}})/P₁(Λ^i_{𝔬_{E_i}}). items.name: Parabolic subgroups of 𝒢°_i realized by refining Λ^i with self-dual flags
items.statement: Let E₁/E₁,₀ and a self-dual 𝔬_{E₁}-lattice sequence Λ¹ of 𝔬_{E₁}-period e in (V¹,f₁) be as in the paper. For a proper parabolic 𝒫°₁ of 𝒢°₁=P°(Λ¹_{𝔬₁})/P₁(Λ¹_{𝔬₁}), there is a self-dual 𝔬₁-lattice sequence Λ′¹ with 𝔟₀(Λ′¹)⊆𝔟₀(Λ¹) whose P°(Λ′¹_{𝔬₁}) has image 𝒫°₁ and whose P₁(Λ′¹_{𝔬₁}) projects onto the unipotent radical 𝒰₁. Construction: 𝒫°₁ is the stabilizer of a self-dual k_{E₁}-flag in Λ¹(0)/Λ¹(1), k_{E₁}-flags in Λ¹(r)/Λ¹(r+1) for 1≤r<e/2, and a self-dual k_{E₁}-flag in Λ¹(⌊(e+1)/2⌋)/Λ¹(⌊e/2⌋+1); the image of Λ′¹ consists of the inverse images of these flags, their duals and their E₁-multiples.

items.name: Representations lying over ϑ (Definition 7.6)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. With PAPER-STEVENS-08/264 and (H): let [Λ′,n′,0,β] be a skew semisimple stratum with 𝔐_{Λ′}=𝔐_Λ (the standard maximal lattice sequence, 𝔐_Λ^i(2r+s)=𝔭_{E_i}^rΛ^i(s), s=0,1) and 𝔟₀(Λ′)⊇𝔟₀(Λ); θ′=τ_{Λ,Λ′,β}θ, η′ its Heisenberg representation, κ′ the unique standard β-extension of η′ compatible with κ, and ρ′ the inflation to J°(β,Λ′) of an irreducible component of Ind_{P°(Λ_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ′_{𝔬_E})}^{P°(Λ′_{𝔬_E})/P₁(Λ′_{𝔬_E})} ρ̄. Then ϑ′=κ′⊗ρ′ is said to lie over ϑ=κ⊗ρ. items.name: Harish-Chandra irreducibility for a maximal parabolic of a finite general linear group
items.statement: Let k be a finite field, 𝒢=GL_{a+b}(k) (more generally a connected finite reductive group with such a factor), 𝒫=𝓛𝒰 the standard maximal parabolic with Levi 𝓛=GL_a(k)×GL_b(k) and 𝒫⁻ its opposite, σ₁, σ₂ irreducible cuspidal representations of GL_a(k), GL_b(k). If σ₁≇σ₂ (automatic when a≠b) then Ind_𝒫^𝒢(σ₁⊗σ₂) (inflated through 𝒫→𝓛) is irreducible; moreover Ind_𝒫^𝒢(σ₁⊗σ₂)≅Ind_{𝒫⁻}^𝒢(σ₁⊗σ₂) (independence of the parabolic), so the unique constituent lies over both.

items.name: [BK2, Theorem 7.2] and the notions it uses: decomposed pairs, strongly positive elements, G-covers
items.statement: Let G be the F₀-points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field, M a Levi subgroup, P=MU a parabolic with opposite P⁻=MU⁻, K compact open, ρ irreducible smooth of K. (K,ρ) is decomposed with respect to (M,P) if K=(K∩U⁻)(K∩M)(K∩U) and K∩U, K∩U⁻⊆ker ρ. An element ζ of the centre of M is strongly (P,K)-positive if ζ(K∩U)ζ⁻¹⊆K∩U, ζ⁻¹(K∩U⁻)ζ⊆K∩U⁻, and for all compact open H₁⊆U, H₂⊆U⁻ some power ζ^r has ζ^rH₁ζ^{−r}⊆K∩U, ζ^{−r}H₂ζ^r⊆K∩U⁻. As used in §7.2: if (K,ρ) is decomposed and H(G,ρ) contains an invertible element supported on KζK with ζ strongly (P,K)-positive, then (K,ρ) is a G-cover of (K∩M,ρ|_{K∩M}); in particular every irreducible π containing ρ has π_U≠0, so is not supercuspidal if M≠G. The same holds if I_G(ρ)⊆KMK (then H(G,ρ)≅H(M,ρ_M) and central elements of M give invertible elements).

items.statement: Let k be a finite field of odd characteristic and ρ̄ an irreducible cuspidal representation of GL_d(k) with ρ̄∘σ≅ρ̄ for σ(g)=ᵗg⁻¹ (equivalently ρ̄≅ρ̄^∨). If d is odd then d=1.
items.locator: Cited in §7.2.2 ('see for example [1, Theorem 7.1]'), arXiv v2 p. 52; bibliography [1] (J. Adler, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 125(8) (1997) 2471–2479)
items.note: Adler's paper was not accessible (AMS returned HTTP 403); its main theorem concerns tamely ramified self-contragredient supercuspidals of GL_n(F) (exist iff n or p even). The finite-field statement used is checked directly: cuspidals of GL_d(k) correspond to Frobenius orbits of regular characters θ of k_d^×; self-duality gives θ⁻¹=θ^{q^i}, forcing d|2i, so for d odd i=0, θ²=1, θ^q=θ, and regularity gives d=1. Tau Ceti has only the GL₂ cuspidal family (CharacterTheory layer 9, GL2Cuspidal); no general Green/Deligne–Lusztig parametrization is planned; not covered by the Part II brief.

items.name: Conclusion: failure of (H) yields a maximal simple type and π≅c-Ind
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, with a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀; (V,h) an N-dimensional F-space with a nondegenerate ε-hermitian form (ε=±1); G⁺ the isometry group (unitary, symplectic or orthogonal over F₀), G the F₀-points of its identity component (G=G⁺ except orthogonal, where G=SO); G̃=Aut_F(V); all representations smooth complex; self-dual lattice sequences normalized so Λ(k)^#=Λ(1−k), periods even. Let π be irreducible supercuspidal. By [S4, Theorem 5.1] and §7.2, π contains ϑ=κ⊗ρ on J°(β,Λ) with κ standard and ρ cuspidal; (H) fails by Propositions 7.10/7.13, so one may take 𝔟₀(Λ) maximal self-dual. Then π contains an irreducible component λ of Ind_{J°(β,Λ)}^{J(β,Λ)}ϑ, λ=κ⊗τ with κ a β-extension and τ a component of Ind_{J°}^{J}ρ (so τ is cuspidal in the sense of Definition 6.17); (J(β,Λ),λ) is a maximal simple type and by Corollary 6.19 c-Ind_J^Gλ is irreducible, hence π≅c-Ind_J^Gλ. CORRECTED (PAPER-STEVENS-08/E3, PAPER-STEVENS-08/E4): Corollary 6.19 requires the Miyauchi–Stevens cuspidal-type conditions (G_E compact centre, P°(Λ_{𝔬_E}) maximal parahoric), which the corrected hypothesis replacing (H) supplies, and G≇SO(1,1)(F).

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations
routes.brief: This route coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartII, proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 1 and joined by PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21, PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B and PAPER-NAKAMURA-23; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. It adds the classical-group branch of Stevens (Invent. Math. 172 (2008)), which the rejected PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24 route 3 could not add because it was unread: F a non-archimedean local field of any characteristic with odd residual characteristic p, a (possibly trivial) Galois involution with fixed field F₀, (V, h) an ε-hermitian space, G⁺ = U(V, h) and G the F₀-points of its identity component (unitary, symplectic, special orthogonal). Final theorems, as corrected by Miyauchi–Stevens (Math. Ann. 358 (2014)): Proposition 6.18 — for a maximal simple type (J_M, λ_M) with G_E of compact centre and P°(Λ^M_{o_E}) a maximal parahoric of G_E, I_G(λ_M) = J_M; Corollary 6.19 — then c-Ind_{J_M}^G λ_M is irreducible supercuspidal and (J_M, λ_M) is a [G, π]_G-type; Theorem 7.14 — for G not the split SO(1,1)(F), every irreducible supercuspidal representation of G is c-Ind_{J_M}^G(κ_M ⊗ τ) for such a type, built from a skew semisimple stratum, a skew semisimple character, its Heisenberg representation, a β-extension and a cuspidal representation τ of the finite reductive quotient. Cover: self-dual lattice sequences and skew semisimple strata with the critical exponent; the self-dual building model and its centralizer embedding; the groups H¹ ⊆ J¹ ⊆ J and skew semisimple characters with transfer; Heisenberg representations and β-extensions (maximal and general case, the G̃ analogues); Iwahori decompositions and factorizations of semisimple characters; Glauberman transfer; the Hecke-algebra isomorphism and Weyl-group elements of §6 with the intertwining of β-extensions; the level-zero Hecke algebra injection (Morris), covers and the exhaustion argument of §7 with Miyauchi–Stevens's replacement of hypothesis (H). Import the smooth category, Hecke algebras, compact induction with Frobenius reciprocity and admissibility/supercuspidality from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0:abelian-category, SR.1, SR.2 and SR.3; buildings, parahorics and the generalized affine BN-pair from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1–RG2.4; the general type/cover formalism and ρ-spherical Hecke algebras from this Part II's Fintzen branch; finite Heisenberg representations from FiniteWeilRepresentationsPartII; the six facts about finite reductive groups used in Lemmas 3.9–3.10, 4.10 and 7.9 and §7.2.2 (commutators of unipotent radicals, SL_2(𝔽_3), characters trivial on unipotents, Harish-Chandra irreducibility for GL_{a+b}(k), self-dual cuspidals of GL_d(k)) from ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 3); and mixed-characteristic GL_m type theory from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6, constructing no second GL_m classification. The Bushnell–Kutzko GL_N simple and semisimple strata/characters Stevens uses are needed in every odd residual characteristic, including equal characteristic, which ET.6 excludes; keep that extension explicit and separately checked, and do not rebuild ET.6's mixed-characteristic case. Keep Fintzen's p ∤ |W| branch and Stevens's odd-p classical branch separate, with a comparison only where both apply. Endo-parameters and L-packets of classical groups are not part of this route. Repairs after RT-STEVENS: use o_{F₀}-lattices and F₀-linear/o_{F₀}-linear maps for skew parts in A₋, while ambient objects and the underlying Λ in V remain over F/o_F. Include the unramified ℚ₃(i) unitary-line scalar-closure and F=F₀ checks. Import the relative Clifford obstruction on K/N from InductionRestriction layer 7; the absolute projective linearization criterion on K/ker η cannot preserve η by itself. Request the finite-quotient/relative determinant bridge: d=dim η and m=ord(det η) are p-powers, (det ρ)^m descends and δ(det ρ)^m=α^(dm); restriction to S/N and prime-to-p transfer then kill the relative class. Keep item 114’s algebraic/continuous carrier comparison explicit. Item 246 is the single disconnected finite-quotient cuspidality predicate; item 306 is merged into it, importing the connected Fintzen /33 predicate for both maximal-order and §§7.2–7.3 uses.
routes.reason: Stevens proves that every supercuspidal representation of a p-adic classical group with p odd is compactly induced from an explicit type, the classical-group analogue of Bushnell–Kutzko. Nothing in the atlas plans lattice sequences, skew semisimple strata and characters, β-extensions or these types: SR.0–SR.6 stop at the general smooth theory, RG2 supplies buildings, and ET.6 is mixed-characteristic GL_m. The accepted SmoothRepresentationsPartII (Fintzen's tame p ∤ |W| construction) is exactly the direction — types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations — but its hypotheses exclude p ≤ rank for classical groups, and its accepted brief does not contain Stevens's construction; the GHSB attempt to add it was rejected only because the paper had not been read. This extraction reads it, so the classical-group branch joins the same Part II rather than a new roadmap, as the maintainer's note asks.

routes.title: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels, Part II: finite Weil–Heisenberg representations
routes.brief: This route coalesces with FiniteWeilRepresentationsPartII, proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 3; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Stevens uses two finite Heisenberg statements, for p odd: (1) for a finite p-group J with H ⊴ J, J/H elementary abelian and a J-stable character θ of H whose commutator pairing J/H × J/H → μ_p is nondegenerate, there is a unique irreducible η containing θ, with η|_H = θ^{⊕(J:H)^{1/2}} (Proposition 3.5, with a cyclic centre of order p^a, not only p); (2) the isotropic-induction form: for Q/Z = W₀ ⊥ (W₋ ⊕ W₊) with W_± totally isotropic and dual, and U₊ lifting W₊ with θ trivial on U₊ ∩ Z, the representation η_P of the preimage of W₀ ⊕ W₊ containing θ_P is unique, η ≅ Ind η_P, and η_P is the U₊-invariants of η (Corollary 5.7, Lemma 5.12). Add these to the finite Weil–Heisenberg layer with their exact hypotheses, reuse its Stone–von Neumann theorem, and export them to SmoothRepresentationsPartII's classical-group branch; import finite-group induction and Mackey theory from Tau Ceti's representation-theory roadmaps.
routes.reason: The two lemmas are finite-group statements about Heisenberg groups, exactly the direction of the accepted FiniteWeilRepresentationsPartII (Fintzen route 3), whose items assume a centre of order p; Stevens needs the cyclic-centre and isotropic-induction forms. They belong there, not in the p-adic Part II.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: modular representations and generic GL3 lattices
routes.brief: This route coalesces with ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups, the Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups roadmap proposed by PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-20 (route accepted), reused by PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 and joined by PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 route 2 for the Harish-Chandra theory of finite classical groups; keep its id, parent, title and area. Stevens (Invent. Math. 172 (2008); arXiv:math/0607622v2) uses six facts about finite reductive groups over a finite field k of odd characteristic, all general finite-group statements. (1) [Digne–Michel, p. 129]: for a Borel subgroup ℬ = 𝒯𝒰 of a connected reductive group over k, [𝒰, 𝒰] = ∏_{α∈Σ⁺∖Δ} 𝒰_α (relative roots in the non-split case), outside the small-field exceptions B_2 and F_4 over 𝔽_2 and G_2 over 𝔽_2 and 𝔽_3 (the paper omits G_2 over 𝔽_2, E15), so every character of 𝒰 is a product of characters of the simple root groups. (2) For the finite classical groups that occur, a character of 𝒰 intertwined by the whole group is trivial, except on SL_2(𝔽_3) factors (the claim in the proof of Lemma 3.9). (3) SL_2(𝔽_3) = Q ⋊ 𝒰 with Q ≅ Q_8 its normal Sylow 2-subgroup, so every character of 𝒰 ≅ 𝔽_3 extends to SL_2(𝔽_3) and the non-trivial extensions are cuspidal. (4) A character of the rational points of a possibly disconnected reductive group over k that is trivial on all unipotent subgroups and on a rational parabolic of the identity component is trivial on the identity component (proof of Lemma 4.10). (5) Harish-Chandra irreducibility for a maximal parabolic of GL_{a+b}(k): for cuspidal σ_1, σ_2 of GL_a(k), GL_b(k) with σ_1 ≇ σ_2, Ind_𝒫(σ_1 ⊗ σ_2) is irreducible and independent of the parabolic with Levi GL_a × GL_b (proof of Lemma 7.9). (6) A self-dual cuspidal representation of GL_d(k) has d = 1 or d even (cited from Adler in §7.2.2). Prove them in this generality, with (5) and (6) from the Harish-Chandra and Green theory this roadmap builds for PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20. Import: rational BN-pairs and Borel subgroups of finite reductive groups from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups (layer 7 plans Bruhat decomposition and Tits systems); Tau Ceti's abstract Tits systems (TauCeti.TitsSystem) and Mackey criterion (TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_iff_doubleCoset); GL_2(𝔽_q) from Tau Ceti CharacterTheory layer 9, where TauCeti.simple_GL2PrincipalSeries_iff is the case a = b = 1 of (5). The consumer is SmoothRepresentationsPartII (route 1): Lemmas 3.9–3.10, 4.10 and 7.9 and §7.2.2 of the paper.
routes.reason: These six items are statements about finite reductive groups, not about p-adic groups; the extraction itself notes that SmoothRepresentationsPartII (whose accepted brief needs no Deligne–Lusztig or Harish-Chandra theory) does not supply them. PROTOCOL.md §15 gives such facts one owner, the most foundational roadmap that plans finite reductive groups: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups, which the LLHLM extractions make the single foundation for Deligne–Lusztig theory and to which PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 route 2 sends Green's classification and the Harish-Chandra theory of finite classical groups. The route joins it with its id, parent, title and area unchanged.

sourceIssues.printed: The introduction says E=F[β] is a sum of fields, each stable under the involution, and identifies this with β being elliptic semisimple in the Lie algebra of G. In §1 (ii), it asserts compactness of the G-normalizer of P for the classical groups under consideration.
sourceIssues.correction: Both fail when G is orthogonal (F = F₀, ε = +1) and the null block V⁰ (β₀ = 0) has dimension 2 with h|V⁰ isotropic: then G_E has the factor SO(V⁰) = SO(1,1)(F) ≅ F^×, a split central torus, so β is not elliptic, and the maximal parahoric o_F^× of that factor has non-compact normalizer F^×. The correct condition is that G_E has compact centre.
sourceIssues.reason: SO(1,1)(F) = {diag(t, t⁻¹)} in a hyperbolic basis is ≅ F^×, commutes with β (β acts by 0 on V⁰) and lies in the centre of G_E = ∏ G_{E_i}; its maximal compact subgroup o_F^× is normal in F^×. Miyauchi–Stevens state that a factor SO(1,1)(F) of G_E 'can only happen when G is an even-dimensional orthogonal group and β_i = 0, dim_F V^i = 2' and add 'G_E has compact centre' to the definition of cuspidal type for this reason. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Miyauchi–Stevens 2014.)

sourceIssues.locator: Introduction, arXiv v2 pp. 3-4 (TeX 555-564); = Definition 6.17 / Proposition 6.18 / Corollary 6.19, pp. 43-44 (TeX 3800-3864)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that maximal compactness of P(Λ_{o_E}) in G_E makes the intertwining of λ equal to J(β,Λ). For any irreducible τ on J(β,Λ) containing a cuspidal ρ upon restriction to J°(β,Λ), it concludes π = c-Ind_{J(β,Λ)}^G(κ⊗τ) is irreducible and therefore supercuspidal. sourceIssues.correction: Require that G_E have compact centre and that P°(Λ_{o_E}) be a maximal parahoric subgroup of G_E (Miyauchi–Stevens's definition of cuspidal type); then Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19 hold with the same proof.
sourceIssues.reason: (1) Miyauchi–Stevens: for G_E a quasi-split ramified unitary group in 2 variables, one of the two maximal self-dual o_E-orders gives P°(Λ_{o_E}) an Iwahori subgroup; then P°/P₁ is a torus, every irreducible representation of it is cuspidal, and the construction does not give a supercuspidal type (for β = 0 it gives a depth-zero principal-series type). sourceIssues.correction: Exclude G = SO(1,1)(F) ≅ F^× (F = F₀, ε = +1, dim_F V = 2, h isotropic), as Miyauchi–Stevens do; for every other G in the class the centre of G is compact and the theorem holds (with cuspidal types as in PAPER-STEVENS-08/E2).
sourceIssues.reason: For G = SO(1,1)(F) ≅ F^× every irreducible representation is a character, and a character is supercuspidal (G has no proper parabolic subgroup); but c-Ind_J^G λ for J compact open is infinite-dimensional, since G/J is infinite. So no supercuspidal of G is compactly induced from a compact open subgroup. The paper's closing sentence (p. 53) says 'compact (mod-centre) subgroups', which is true for this G. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Miyauchi–Stevens 2014.)

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, proofs of Lemma 2.10 (arXiv v2 p. 12, TeX 1206-1210) and Lemma 2.12 (p. 12, TeX 1247)
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.10 asserts local constancy of Λ″ ↦ a₀(Λ″) along the segment except at a discrete, hence finite, set: its intersections with building walls. Lemma 2.12 asserts that deleting every building wall from [Λ,Λ′,Λ″] partitions it into disjoint convex polygons.
sourceIssues.correction: Use only the walls of I(G̃, F₀) that do not contain the segment (resp. the affine plane of the triangle). Walls containing it do not separate its points, and the rest of each proof is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: The image of I(G̃_E, F₀) often lies inside walls of I(G̃, F₀). Example: V = V¹ ⊕ V², dim_F V^i = 2, E_i/F unramified quadratic; in an adapted apartment of GL₄(F) the points of I(G̃_E) are (a,a,b,b), which lie on the walls x₁ − x₂ = 0 and x₃ − x₄ = 0, and b₀ = o_{E₁} ⊕ o_{E₂} is constant. The segment from (0,0,0,0) to (1/2,1/2,0,0) meets a wall at every point, so the literal set of the proof is the whole segment and 'removing all walls' leaves nothing. The segments and triangles used in §4 lie in the image of I(G̃_E, F₀), so they are of this kind whenever some E_i/F has residue degree > 1.

sourceIssues.reason: Chevalley commutator formula for G_2 (a short, b long) over F_2, where 2 = 0 and 3 = 1: [x_a,x_b] ∈ x_{a+b}x_{2a+b}U_{3a+b}U_{3a+2b}, [x_a,x_{a+b}] ∈ U_{3a+b}U_{3a+2b}, [x_a,x_{2a+b}] ∈ U_{3a+b}, [x_b,x_{3a+b}], [x_{a+b},x_{2a+b}] ∈ U_{3a+2b}, other pairs commute. (G_2(2) is not quasi-simple, but neither is B_2(2) ≅ S_6, which the paper lists, so '(quasi-simple)' refers to the type.) requests.statement: Let N ⊴ K be open pro-p in a profinite group, with invariant irreducible smooth η of finite p-power dimension d. Smoothness and finite dimension make ker η open in N; invariance makes it normal in K, so K/ker η is finite and N/ker η is a finite p-group. Thus m=ord(det η) is a p-power. For the normalized relative lift ρ of item 112 put D(k)=det ρ(k). Since D(nk)=det η(n)D(k), D^m descends to a normalized cochain D̄_m:K/N→ℂˣ. Taking determinants in the factor-set identity yields δD̄_m=α^(dm), so dm[α]=0 on K/N. This is the relative p-primary bound; the bound d[α]=0 alone is generally false there.
